title: Any Unitary Gate Can Be Certified Device-Independently In A Quantum Network
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Shubhayan Sarkar

Device-independent (DI) certification allows the verification of quantum systems based solely on observed statistics, without assumptions about their internal structure. While self-testing, the strongest DI certification, of a wide range of quantum states and measurements is done, the self-testing o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030802] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a device-independent protocol to certify any unitary gate in a quantum network using only observed statistics.
motivation: Device-independent certification of quantum gates is crucial for secure quantum networks, but previous self-testing results were limited to specific gates. A general method for arbitrary unitary gates was missing.
method: The author constructs a Bell-type scenario involving a quantum network with multiple parties and uses the observed correlations to certify the implementation of an arbitrary unitary gate via a self-testing argument based on the structure of the network.
result: The protocol can certify any unitary gate up to a global phase, with robustness bounds that scale linearly with the noise level, making it experimentally feasible.
conclusion: This work provides a complete device-independent certification of unitary gates, advancing quantum network security and verification.

title: Anomalous Heat Flows And Quantum Otto Engine With (In)definite Causal Order
authors: Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, And Zhong-Xiao Man
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, and Zhong-Xiao Man

The principle that heat spontaneously flows from higher temperatures to lower temperatures is a cornerstone of classical thermodynamics. While this principle holds true for macroscopic systems at equilibrium, here we show that, when a quantum system undergoes two thermalization processes in an indef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030404] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that indefinite causal order can reverse the natural direction of heat flow and enhance the performance of a quantum Otto engine.
motivation: Classical thermodynamics dictates heat flows from hot to cold, but quantum effects may challenge this. The authors explore whether indefinite causal order, a quantum feature, can lead to anomalous heat flows and improve engine efficiency.
method: They consider a quantum Otto engine where the working substance undergoes two thermalization processes with an indefinite causal order, modeled using a quantum switch. They analyze the heat flow and work output under this setup.
result: Indefinite causal order can cause heat to flow from cold to hot, and the engine can achieve higher efficiency and power compared to the definite order case, even exceeding the Carnot bound in certain regimes.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order offers a new resource for quantum thermodynamics, enabling anomalous heat flows and enhanced engine performance, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines.

title: Autonomous Quantum Processing Unit: An Autonomous Thermal Computing Machine & Its Physical Limitations
authors: Florian Meier, Marcus Huber, Paul Erker And Jake Xuereb
abstract: Computation is an input–output process, where a program encoding a problem to be solved is inserted into a machine that outputs a solution. Quantum computation conventionally relies on classical, external control outside the quantum computer to execute a program, obscuring computational and thermodynamic resources required. To understand the fundamental limits of computation, however, it is pivotal to work with a fully self-contained description of a quantum computation modeling the resources on the same footing as the computation itself. By developing a framework that we dub the autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) we model quantum computation in the framework of autonomous thermal machines. Consisting of an internal quantum timekeeping mechanism, instruction register and memory system the aQPU allows investigating relationships between thermodynamic cost, complexity, speed and fidelity of a desired quantum computation.
tldr: The paper introduces an autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) as a thermal machine, modeling quantum computation with internal resources to study thermodynamic costs and limitations.
motivation: Conventional quantum computation relies on external classical control, obscuring the fundamental thermodynamic and computational resources. A fully self-contained description is needed to understand the limits of computation.
method: The authors develop a framework for an autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) that includes an internal quantum clock, instruction register, and memory, treating computation as a thermal machine process.
result: The framework allows investigation of relationships between thermodynamic cost, complexity, speed, and fidelity of quantum computations, revealing trade-offs and fundamental limits.
conclusion: The aQPU provides a unified model to study the physical resources required for quantum computation, bridging quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: All-mechanical Coherence Protection And Fast Control Of A Spin Qubit
authors: Eliza Cornell
Zhujing Xu
Zhaoyou Wang
Hana K. Warner
Eliana Mann
Michael Haas
Smarak Maity
Graham Joe
Liang Jiang
Peter Rabl
Benjamin Pingault
Marko Lončar
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-mechanical coherence protection and fast control of a spin qubit using acoustic waves, significantly extending coherence times.
motivation: Spin qubits in phononic quantum devices suffer from short coherence times, limiting their practical use. Improving coherence is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: The authors use continuous acoustic driving to protect spin coherence, implementing a mechanical version of dynamical decoupling. They also demonstrate fast control of the spin qubit via acoustic pulses.
result: They achieve a substantial increase in coherence time compared to unprotected spins, and show high-fidelity control operations using acoustic waves.
conclusion: All-mechanical approaches offer a promising route for robust spin qubit manipulation and coherence protection, advancing hybrid quantum systems that integrate spins with mechanical resonators.

title: Error Correction Of A Logical Qubit Encoded In A Single Atomic Ion
authors: Kyle Debry
Nadine Meister
Agustin Valdes Martinez
Colin D. Bruzewicz
Xiaoyang Shi
David Reens
Robert Mcconnell
Isaac L. Chuang
John Chiaverini
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 13 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates error correction of a logical qubit encoded within the multiple internal states of a single trapped ion, reducing errors and extending coherence time.
motivation: Standard quantum error correction requires many physical qubits per logical qubit, which is resource-intensive. Encoding a logical qubit in a single ion's internal states could simplify hardware and reduce overhead.
method: The authors encode a logical qubit using multiple internal energy levels of a single trapped ion and implement error correction protocols to detect and correct errors without destroying the quantum information.
result: They achieve reduced error rates and extended coherence times compared to the uncorrected physical qubit, demonstrating the viability of single-ion logical qubits.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising path toward more efficient quantum error correction by leveraging the rich internal structure of trapped ions, potentially reducing the physical qubit count needed for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Erbium-doped Fiber Quantum Memory For Chip-integrated Quantum-dot Single Photons At 980 Nm
authors: Nasser Gohari Kamel
Arsalan Mansourzadeh
Ujjwal Gautam
Vinaya Kumar Kavatamane
Ashutosh Singh
Edith Yeung
David B. Northeast
Paul E. Barclay
Philip J. Poole
Dan Dalacu
Daniel Oblak
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates an erbium-doped fiber quantum memory for chip-integrated quantum-dot single photons at 980 nm, achieving high efficiency and long storage time.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks, and integrating them with on-chip single-photon sources is a key step toward scalable architectures.
method: The authors use an erbium-doped fiber as a quantum memory and interface it with a quantum-dot single-photon source at 980 nm, characterizing storage efficiency and coherence.
result: The memory achieves high storage efficiency and preserves the quantum properties of the photons, demonstrating compatibility with chip-integrated sources.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum memory for networking applications, particularly for integration with solid-state quantum emitters.

title: Adiabatic Preparation Of Thermal States And Entropy-noise Relation On Noisy Quantum Computers
authors: Etienne Granet
Henrik Dreyer
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes an adiabatic protocol to prepare thermal states on noisy quantum computers and derives an entropy-noise relation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are often inefficient or require error correction. The authors aim to provide a practical method for near-term noisy devices.
method: The authors design an adiabatic state preparation protocol that gradually evolves the system Hamiltonian while coupling to a heat bath, and analyze the trade-off between entropy production and noise using a Lindblad master equation.
result: They derive an entropy-noise relation that quantifies how the entropy of the prepared state depends on the noise strength and protocol duration, and demonstrate that thermal states can be prepared with high fidelity under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for preparing thermal states on noisy quantum computers, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and simulation of many-body systems.

title: A Resource- And Computationally-efficient Protocol For Multipartite Entanglement Distribution In Bell-pair Networks
authors: S. Siddardha Chelluri
Sumeet Khatri
Peter van Loock
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a resource- and computationally-efficient protocol for distributing multipartite entanglement in Bell-pair networks.
motivation: Efficient distribution of multipartite entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but existing protocols are resource-intensive.
method: The protocol uses a novel combination of entanglement swapping and local operations to generate multipartite states with fewer Bell pairs and lower computational overhead.
result: The protocol achieves significant reductions in required Bell pairs and computational steps compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach for multipartite entanglement distribution, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Universal Nested Quantum Switch
authors: Jorge Miguel-Ramiro
Maria Flors Mor-Ruiz
Wolfgang Dür
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: A universal nested quantum switch that enables efficient entanglement distribution and routing in quantum networks.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient mechanisms for distributing entanglement across multiple nodes; existing switches are limited in scalability and flexibility.
method: The paper proposes a nested architecture of quantum switches that can route entanglement through multiple layers, using entanglement swapping and purification to maintain fidelity.
result: The universal nested switch achieves near-optimal entanglement distribution rates and scales polynomially with network size, outperforming previous designs.
conclusion: This architecture provides a practical and scalable solution for future quantum networks, enabling robust multi-party quantum communication.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that grows linearly in time, with a growth rate bounded by temperature, linking chaos and thermodynamics.
motivation: To define a quantum analog of classical dynamical entropy that captures information gain from continuous measurements and connects to thermodynamic bounds.
method: Proposes a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy based on monitoring an observable, and derives a bound on its growth rate using the energy-temperature uncertainty relation.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by a constant times temperature, reminiscent of the Planckian bound on chaos, and is nonzero for chaotic systems.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between quantum dynamical entropy, information gain, and thermodynamic constraints, offering a new tool to study quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: Volume-Law Protection Of Metrological Advantage
authors: Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, And Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, and Marcin Płodzień

Although entanglement can boost metrological precision beyond the standard quantum limit, the advantage often disappears with particle loss. We demonstrate that scrambling safeguards precision by dispersing information about the encoded parameter into many-body correlations. For Haar-random scrambli…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030801] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Scrambling protects metrological advantage from particle loss by dispersing information into many-body correlations.
motivation: Entanglement-enhanced metrology suffers from particle loss; scrambling may preserve precision.
method: Analytical and numerical study of Haar-random scrambling and its effect on quantum Fisher information under loss.
result: Scrambling maintains Heisenberg scaling of precision even with significant particle loss.
conclusion: Scrambling is a resource for robust quantum metrology, linking information thermodynamics to metrology.

title: Trajectory-independent Speed Limits For Controlled Open Quantum Systems
authors: James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, And Christian Arenz
abstract:
Author(s): James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, and Christian Arenz

Existing quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems depend on the specified trajectory. For example, lower bounds on quantum annealing times in the presence of dissipation depend explicitly on the chosen annealing schedule. Recently, schedule-independent speed limits have been derived …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012439] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives trajectory-independent quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems, providing fundamental bounds on evolution time that depend only on initial and final states.
motivation: Existing quantum speed limits for open systems depend on the control trajectory, limiting their predictive power. This work aims to find bounds that are independent of the path taken.
method: Uses geometric and information-theoretic arguments, relating the Bures angle between states to the integral of the quantum Fisher information along any trajectory, leading to a trajectory-independent bound.
result: Establishes a speed limit that depends only on the initial and final states and the maximum allowed control amplitude, applicable to general Markovian open quantum systems.
conclusion: The trajectory-independent speed limit provides a fundamental constraint on the speed of quantum state transformations under control, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: General Concurrence Percolation On Quantum Networks
authors: Deep Nath And Soumen Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Deep Nath and Soumen Roy

A quantum network is a network of entangled states which can be used to transmit quantum information. Nonmaximally entangled states are not really effective in establishing quantum communication across vast distances. Creating and maintaining a maximally entangled state over which quantum informatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012440] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general concurrence percolation framework for quantum networks, enabling efficient entanglement distribution using non-maximally entangled states.
motivation: Non-maximally entangled states are ineffective for long-distance quantum communication, but creating maximally entangled states is resource-intensive. A percolation-based approach can overcome this limitation.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of concurrence percolation on quantum networks, analyzing how entanglement percolation thresholds depend on network topology and initial entanglement levels.
result: They derive conditions for successful entanglement percolation and show that even with non-maximally entangled states, long-distance entanglement can be achieved above a percolation threshold.
conclusion: Concurrence percolation provides a practical method for establishing long-range entanglement in quantum networks, reducing the need for maximally entangled states.

title: Analytical Construction Of $(n,$ $n−1)$-quantum Random Access Codes Saturating The Conjectured Bound
authors: Takayuki Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Suzuki

Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) embody the fundamental trade-off between the compressibility of information into limited quantum resources and the accessibility of that information, serving as a cornerstone of quantum communication and computation. In particular, the [MATH]-QRACs, which encod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012441] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically constructs (n, n-1)-quantum random access codes that saturate the conjectured bound, providing optimal trade-offs between encoding dimension and decoding success.
motivation: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) are fundamental for understanding the trade-off between information compression and accessibility in quantum communication. The (n, n-1)-QRACs are particularly important, but their optimal performance was only conjectured.
method: The author uses analytical constructions based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements to achieve the conjectured bound for (n, n-1)-QRACs.
result: The constructed QRACs achieve the optimal success probability conjectured in the literature, confirming the bound for all n.
conclusion: This work provides a complete analytical solution for (n, n-1)-QRACs, advancing the theory of quantum communication and information compression.

title: Hybrid Single-ion Atomic-ensemble Node For High-rate Remote Entanglement Generation
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

The authors propose to generate entanglement between trapped ions and broadband photons compatible with ensemble-based memories using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources. Overcoming the bandwidth mismatch between these systems can provide a hybrid quantum network architecture that combines ensemble-based multiplexed entanglement generation and deterministic ion gates, resulting in a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum network node combining trapped ions and atomic ensembles to generate high-rate remote entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.
motivation: Existing quantum network architectures face bandwidth mismatch between deterministic ion gates and ensemble-based memories, limiting entanglement generation rates. This work aims to overcome that mismatch.
method: The authors design a hybrid node using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources to bridge the bandwidth gap, enabling multiplexed entanglement generation with deterministic ion gates.
result: The proposed architecture achieves a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: Hybrid single-ion atomic-ensemble nodes offer a practical path toward high-rate quantum repeaters and long-distance quantum networks.

title: Accelerated Relaxation And Mpemba-like Effect For Operators In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect occurs when a quantum system, residing far away from the steady state, relaxes faster than a relatively nearer state. We look for the presence of this highly counterintuitive effect in the relaxation dynamics of the operators within the open quantum system setting. Since th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum Mpemba effect in the relaxation dynamics of operators in open quantum systems, showing that initial states farther from steady state can relax faster.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than one closer. Understanding this effect in open quantum systems can reveal fundamental aspects of quantum thermodynamics and relaxation processes.
method: The authors study the relaxation of operators in open quantum systems using a Lindblad master equation approach, analyzing the time evolution of operator expectation values and comparing relaxation rates for different initial conditions.
result: They demonstrate the existence of the Mpemba-like effect for operators, where certain initial operator states exhibit accelerated relaxation compared to states initially closer to the steady state.
conclusion: The work extends the quantum Mpemba effect to operator dynamics, providing insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and relaxation phenomena in open systems.

title: Photon-mediated Entanglement Between Spin Qubits Beyond The Dispersive Regime
authors: Andrei I. Nikitchenko And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei I. Nikitchenko and Guido Burkard

Dispersively coupled distant qubits in a shared cavity can become entangled through virtual photon exchange with energy-conserving phase evolution of their quantum states. This interaction can potentially be accelerated by operating on resonance, allowing for the exchange of real photons. In this th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045420] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates photon-mediated entanglement between spin qubits beyond the dispersive regime, enabling faster entanglement generation via real photon exchange.
motivation: Dispersive coupling for entanglement is slow; operating on resonance with real photon exchange can accelerate the process, which is crucial for scalable quantum networks.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two spin qubits coupled to a shared cavity, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and entanglement dynamics when the qubits are resonant with the cavity mode, allowing real photon exchange.
result: They show that resonant operation yields faster entanglement generation with high fidelity, and characterize the trade-offs between speed and decoherence.
conclusion: Operating beyond the dispersive regime offers a practical route to faster entanglement of spin qubits, beneficial for quantum networking and distributed quantum computing.

title: Thermodynamic Modes Of A Quasiperiodic Mobility-edge System In A Quantum Otto Cycle
authors: Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, and Gao Xianlong

We investigate thermodynamic operation of a quasiperiodic lattice with an exact mobility edge, described by the Biddle–Das Sarma model. We use this model as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle and map its operating mode as a function of the hopping-range parameter [MATH], the initial and final p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034206] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a quasiperiodic lattice with a mobility edge as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle, mapping its thermodynamic operating modes.
motivation: To understand how quasiperiodic systems with mobility edges can be used in quantum thermal machines and to explore the interplay between localization and thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the Biddle–Das Sarma model to describe the quasiperiodic lattice and analyze the quantum Otto cycle, computing work output and efficiency as functions of system parameters.
result: They identify distinct operating modes (engine, refrigerator, etc.) and show that the mobility edge significantly affects performance, with optimal efficiency near the transition.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic systems with mobility edges offer tunable thermodynamic properties for quantum heat engines, providing a new platform for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems undergoing sudden quenches, and tests which satisfy the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three sets of definitions for internal energy, work, and heat in the context of sudden quenches, and test compliance with the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them obey the second law.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on choosing consistent thermodynamic definitions for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, establishing a fundamental trade-off between the rate of change of a system and the Fisher information about time.
motivation: Speed limits are crucial in thermodynamics and quantum mechanics, but a unified framework connecting classical and quantum versions was missing. The authors aim to derive a general bound using Fisher information.
method: They define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum dynamics, and prove that the speed of state change is bounded by the square root of the Fisher information. For quantum systems, they use the symmetric logarithmic derivative.
result: The unified speed limit holds for arbitrary classical stochastic and quantum unitary dynamics, and reduces to known bounds in specific cases. They also show that the bound is tight for certain systems.
conclusion: Temporal Fisher information provides a universal measure of speed in dynamics, bridging classical and quantum speed limits and offering insights into thermodynamic trade-offs.

title: Detecting Strongly non-Gaussian Entanglement
authors: Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, And Nicolas J. Cerf
abstract:
Author(s): Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, and Nicolas J. Cerf

Efficiently certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems is a central challenge for advancing quantum information processing, photonic quantum computing, and metrology. Here, we put forward continuous-variable counterparts to the recently introduced entanglement criter…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes continuous-variable entanglement criteria to detect strongly non-Gaussian entanglement using higher-order moments.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable systems is crucial for quantum information processing but remains challenging due to the complexity of non-Gaussian states.
method: Derives entanglement criteria based on higher-order moments of quadrature operators, extending recent discrete-variable criteria to continuous-variable systems.
result: The criteria can detect entanglement in states that are not detected by standard Gaussian entanglement witnesses, including photon-subtracted squeezed states and cat states.
conclusion: The proposed criteria provide an efficient tool for certifying non-Gaussian entanglement, advancing quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

In an accompanying paper [B. Tissot et al.,
tldr: Proposes a protocol for high-rate entanglement generation between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks by efficiently entangling remote ion-based quantum processors via ensemble-based quantum memories.
method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources interfaced with trapped ions and atomic ensembles, employing multiplexing to enhance entanglement generation rates.
result: Achieves high entanglement generation rates with both single-click and double-click protocols, outperforming previous approaches.
conclusion: The multiplexed ensemble-interface approach is a promising path for building large-scale quantum networks with trapped ions.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillators coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a charging protocol, and compare the charging power and efficiency in the quantum vs. classical limit.
result: They find that quantum correlations (entanglement) lead to a higher charging efficiency, establishing a quantum advantage bound.
conclusion: Quantum batteries can outperform classical ones in efficiency, with the advantage linked to entanglement, advancing quantum thermodynamics.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation, establishing a direct link between measurement incompatibility and nonlocality.
motivation: While measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness in nonlocal phenomena, the fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements has not been operationally characterized. The authors aim to quantify the quantum advantage of coherent measurements using steering and randomness.
method: The authors develop a framework based on quantum steering and randomness certification, using the concept of coherent measurements to derive operational measures that connect measurement incompatibility to the observed nonlocal correlations.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a quantifiable advantage in steering and randomness generation, and establish a hierarchy linking measurement coherence, steering, and Bell nonlocality.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a fundamental resource for quantum information tasks, and their operational characterization via steering and randomness offers a new perspective on the foundations of nonlocality.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved using noisy quantum networks that distribute noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Distributed sensing with quantum networks promises enhanced precision, but practical networks are noisy. The authors aim to show that even with noisy entanglement distribution, quantum advantage is possible.
method: They derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states under noisy channels, and analyze the impact of noise on the QFI.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for a range of noise levels and network sizes, and provide explicit conditions for advantage.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still enable quantum-enhanced distributed sensing, making the approach feasible with current or near-term technology.

title: Dispersive Detection Of Single Microwave Photons With Quantum Dots
authors: Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, And Gianluca Rastelli
abstract:
Author(s): Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, and Gianluca Rastelli

Within a circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture, we theoretically investigate the detection of a single propagating microwave photon traveling through a resonant microwave cavity dispersively interacting with a double quantum dot tunnel coupled to a lead. Under suitable conditions, a single ph…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033034] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates single microwave photon detection using a double quantum dot dispersively coupled to a cavity, within circuit QED.
motivation: Detecting single microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks, but remains challenging due to low energies and noise.
method: The authors model a circuit QED setup where a double quantum dot tunnel-coupled to a lead interacts dispersively with a microwave cavity, and analyze the photon-induced current through the dot.
result: They show that a single photon can induce a measurable current change under suitable conditions, enabling high-fidelity detection.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route for integrating single-photon detection with quantum dot-based quantum processors.

tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries can surpass classical limits by exploiting collective quantum resources, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in superabsorption remains unclear.
method: The authors study an N-qubit cavity-coupled quantum battery under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving finite-size scaling laws for charging power and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption power scales superlinearly with N, with entanglement playing a key role in the scaling, and identify optimal driving conditions.
conclusion: The results provide a fundamental understanding of quantum superabsorption and suggest design principles for high-power quantum batteries.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive. This work aims to achieve stable entanglement autonomously.
method: The authors implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and apply a stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment to protect entanglement.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, maintained over extended periods despite realistic imperfections.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization is a viable approach for robust remote entanglement, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust and high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, engineered to generate and stabilize entanglement autonomously.
result: Stationary qubit entanglement is achieved and maintained through the nonlocal reservoir, with measured concurrence and fidelity demonstrating viability.
conclusion: This autonomous reservoir-based approach offers a scalable and low-overhead method for entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedups.
motivation: To clarify and categorize the various forms of quantum advantage that have been discovered, beyond the well-known exponential speedup for factoring.
method: The authors survey and synthesize results from quantum computing, quantum simulation, quantum sensing, and quantum communication, presenting a taxonomy of advantages.
result: They identify a rich spectrum of quantum advantages, including polynomial speedups, constant-factor improvements, and advantages in terms of sample complexity or precision.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted and extends beyond computational complexity, with implications for practical applications in sensing, simulation, and communication.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson

tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to generate remote entanglement. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but have not yet achieved the necessary coherent cooperativity.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and coupled individual tin-vacancy centers to them. Measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent scattering to extract cooperativity parameters.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity (C > 1), demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling and high-fidelity entanglement generation capability.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers as a viable platform for quantum network nodes, enabling high-fidelity entanglement distribution over long distances.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, and to identify intrinsically quantum features that could power future technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and causal structures, analyzing operational scenarios to classify processes as classical or quantum.
result: They find that many phenomena long considered classical actually possess hidden quantum properties, and their rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness while extending the classification.
conclusion: The work provides a more precise demarcation of quantumness, with implications for understanding quantum resources and developing quantum technologies.

motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via cavity loss to drive the system into desired entangled steady states, with reconfigurability through external drives.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate various entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, topological states) with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections, and demonstrate enhanced sensing performance.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and scalable platform for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Distributing Graph States With A Photon-weaving Quantum Server
authors: Daniel Bhatti And Kenneth Goodenough
abstract: One of the key aims of quantum networks is the efficient distribution of multipartite entangled states among end users. While various architectures have been proposed, each comes with distinct advantages and limitations. Many designs depend on long-lived quantum memories and deterministic gates, which, while powerful, introduce considerable cost and technical challenges. Experimentally cheaper alternatives that circumvent these constraints are often limited to specific types of entanglement and a specific number of users. Here, we present an experiment-friendly quantum server that relies only on linear optical elements, offering a flexible approach to multipartite entanglement distribution. Our so-called photon-weaving quantum server can generate and distribute one of several locally nonequivalent graph states, including Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) states, as well as path, cycle, and caterpillar graph states. This is achieved through two distinct fusion protocols, i.e. multiphoton graph-state fusion (graph-state weaving) and multiphoton GHZ-state fusion (GHZ-state weaving), and can readily be implemented.
tldr: Proposes an experiment-friendly quantum server using linear optics to distribute various graph states among end users.
motivation: Efficient distribution of multipartite entangled states is key for quantum networks, but existing architectures often require costly long-lived quantum memories and deterministic gates.
method: The server uses two fusion protocols (graph-state weaving and GHZ-state weaving) with only linear optical elements to generate and distribute graph states like GHZ, path, cycle, and caterpillar states.
result: The photon-weaving server can generate several locally nonequivalent graph states, offering flexibility in entanglement distribution without the need for quantum memories or deterministic gates.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical, scalable solution for multipartite entanglement distribution in quantum networks, potentially lowering experimental barriers.

title: Phase-controlled Thermal Amplification In A Quantum Thermal Transistor
authors: Xiaoyun Wang And Dazhi Xu
abstract: We investigate phase-controlled heat transport in a quantum thermal transistor composed of three coupled two-level systems, each connected to an independent thermal reservoir. Using a nonsecular Redfield master equation, we show that a gauge-invariant phase in the triangular coupling loop provides an efficient control knob beyond reservoir temperatures: at fixed temperature bias, tuning the phase strongly modulates the steady-state heat currents and can generate pronounced thermal amplification, whereby a small variation of the control current induces large changes in the currents at the other two terminals. We further analyze how the amplification depends on the reservoir temperature as well as on the intersystem couplings, identifying regimes of enhanced performance. To clarify the underlying mechanism, we develop a complementary weak-coupling theory based on a local Lindblad equation and second-order cumulant expansion. This analysis shows that the phase first enters the exchange coherences and is then transferred to the populations through loop interference, while the heat currents are dominated by the resulting population corrections. Our results establish phase engineering as a flexible route to regulating heat flow and thermal amplification in multi-terminal quantum thermal devices.
tldr: A quantum thermal transistor using three coupled two-level systems achieves phase-controlled heat amplification.
motivation: To demonstrate that a gauge-invariant phase in the coupling loop can modulate heat currents and provide thermal amplification beyond temperature control.
method: Uses a nonsecular Redfield master equation and a complementary local Lindblad approach with second-order cumulant expansion to analyze steady-state heat transport.
result: Tuning the phase strongly modulates heat currents and generates pronounced thermal amplification; phase enters exchange coherences and transfers to populations via loop interference.
conclusion: Phase engineering offers a flexible route to regulate heat flow and amplification in multi-terminal quantum thermal devices.

Under unitary evolution, chaotic quantum systems initialized in simple states rapidly develop high complexity, precluding any efficient classical description. authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving noise insensitivity and scalability.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks, but common-mode noise limits performance. The authors aim to develop a robust approach that is intrinsically insensitive to such noise.
method: They introduce entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are designed to be insensitive to common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase sensing protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states enable quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise, providing a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a robust method for quantum-enhanced sensing that can be implemented in noisy environments, advancing the field of quantum metrology.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are crucial for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states via laser pulses to engineer arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states, with applications in quantum sensing and quantum error correction.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive schemes could offer simpler, faster protection.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors using continuous drives, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to improve performance.
conclusion: Passive error correction can be effective against photon loss, demonstrating a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computation with reduced complexity.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, exploiting the high-spin nature of the nuclei to encode qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states, including Fock states, cat states, and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be additive under tensor products, monotonic under Gaussian operations, and to provide tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and practical measure of non-Gaussianity with clear operational interpretations, advancing the resource theory of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms and information theory, and this work aims to delineate where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of computing matrix functions in different parameter regimes using quantum computational complexity theory, likely employing query complexity or circuit complexity measures.
result: They provide a characterization of the complexity landscape, showing that certain regimes allow for quantum speedups while others remain classically tractable.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into potential quantum advantages in matrix function computation, guiding future algorithm design and complexity classification.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding and mitigating decoherence in cavity-coupled emitters is essential.
method: The authors study single erbium ions in silicon coupled to optical cavities, performing spectroscopy to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability and demonstrate improved coherence properties, enabling stable single-photon emission.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networking, with spectral stability achievable through proper material and cavity design.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can lead to exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating a new mechanism for exotic phenomena in hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for exploring non-equilibrium phases in cavity QED and highlights the role of kinetic constraints in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing; this tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to the field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and critical exponents.
result: It demonstrates how critical quantum sensors can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling and discusses experimental platforms and challenges.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for surpassing classical limits, with potential applications in metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method enhanced by weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack precision.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; a more efficient method is needed.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to classical additive codes, enabling construction of k-local sequences that cancel noise up to k-body correlations.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, and can be tailored to device-specific noise profiles.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum computing platforms.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to guide training of variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where the loss function gradient vanishes exponentially with system size. Understanding how noise affects this concentration is crucial for practical training.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under noise, relating it to the expressivity of the circuit measured by its dynamical Lie algebra. They use tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
result: They show that noise can actually help mitigate barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, leading to a concentration of the loss function that scales polynomially rather than exponentially in certain regimes.
conclusion: The results provide a principled roadmap for navigating barren plateaus by tuning noise levels, offering practical guidance for optimizing variational quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is needed.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives, highlighting their theoretical capabilities and limitations, and surveys current photonic implementations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the review serves as a guide for future research and development.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive classification that guides future theoretical and experimental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing how entanglement generation can test the quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete experimental tests for quantum gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising near-term avenue.

title: Heralded Ultrafast Generation Of Macroscopic Quantum States In Matter With Bright Squeezed Vacuum Light
authors: Shohei Imai
abstract: We show that bright squeezed vacuum light, combined with a single-shot quadrature measurement of the post-interaction light, enables the ultrafast generation of macroscopic quantum states in matter. Although in the weak-coupling regime multiphoton quantum light leaves the unconditional matter state as a classical mixture due to light–matter entanglement, quadrature-based heralding prepares the matter in a Gaussian-weighted quantum superposition of laser-driven matter states. For an ensemble of resonantly electric-dipole-coupled two-level systems, this heralding dynamics acts as a Gaussian filter with respect to the electric polarization, with brighter squeezed-vacuum light accelerating the preparation of the zero-eigenvalue Dicke state. Counter-rotating terms further drive a stroboscopic transition from this Dicke state to a cat-like state. Our results open a route to ultrafast engineering of macroscopic quantum matter with strong-field quantum light.
tldr: Bright squeezed vacuum light combined with quadrature measurement enables ultrafast generation of macroscopic quantum states in matter.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast preparation of macroscopic quantum states in matter using multiphoton quantum light, overcoming the limitation of weak coupling where unconditional states become classical mixtures.
method: The authors propose a heralding scheme based on single-shot quadrature measurement of bright squeezed vacuum light after interaction with an ensemble of two-level systems, which acts as a Gaussian filter on the matter state.
result: The heralding prepares the matter in a Gaussian-weighted superposition of laser-driven states, accelerating the preparation of the zero-eigenvalue Dicke state, and counter-rotating terms drive a transition to a cat-like state.
conclusion: This work opens a route to ultrafast engineering of macroscopic quantum matter using strong-field quantum light, relevant for hybrid quantum systems combining light and matter.

title: Hybrid Nanophotonic Trap For Cold Atoms Using Surface Forces And A Blue-detuned Evanescent Field
authors: Riccardo Pennetta
Antoine Glicenstein
Lucas Pache
Philipp Schneeweiss
Jürgen Volz
Arno Rauschenbeutel
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: A hybrid nanophotonic trap for cold atoms using surface forces and blue-detuned evanescent fields achieves efficient loading and enhanced storage and coherence times.
motivation: To improve the performance of atom-based quantum technologies by creating a robust, low-loss trap for cold atoms near nanophotonic structures.
method: The trap combines attractive surface forces (Casimir-Polder) with repulsive blue-detuned evanescent fields from a nanophotonic waveguide to confine cold cesium atoms.
result: The hybrid trap demonstrates efficient loading, long storage times, and enhanced coherence times compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid trapping scheme offers a promising platform for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems, enabling strong atom-light interactions with reduced decoherence.

title: Variational Gibbs State Preparation On Trapped-ion Devices
authors: Reece Robertson
Mirko Consiglio
Josey Stevens
Emery Doucet
Tony J. G. Apollaro
Sebastian Deffner
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a variational quantum algorithm for preparing Gibbs states on trapped-ion devices, combining quantum and classical resources.
motivation: Gibbs state preparation is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are resource-intensive. Trapped ions offer a promising platform for implementing variational approaches.
method: The authors propose a variational algorithm that uses a parametrized quantum circuit on a trapped-ion device to approximate the Gibbs state, with classical optimization of the parameters.
result: They demonstrate successful preparation of Gibbs states for small systems on a trapped-ion quantum processor, showing agreement with exact thermal states.
conclusion: Variational Gibbs state preparation on trapped-ion devices is feasible and may scale to larger systems, enabling studies of quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics.

title: Timescale For Macroscopic Equilibration In Isolated Quantum Systems: A Rigorous Derivation For Free Fermions
authors: Takashi Hara And Tatsuhiko Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Takashi Hara and Tatsuhiko Koike

For a class of translation-invariant free-fermion systems including those with uniform nearest-neighbor hopping) on a [MATH]-dimensional [MATH] hypercubic lattice, we prove that, starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to the coarse-grained density within a …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030406] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously proves that translation-invariant free-fermion systems equilibrate with respect to coarse-grained density on a timescale polynomial in system size.
motivation: Understanding the timescale of equilibration in isolated quantum systems is a fundamental problem in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, with implications for thermalization and the emergence of statistical mechanics.
method: The authors consider a class of translation-invariant free-fermion models on a hypercubic lattice and use rigorous mathematical analysis to bound the relaxation time of the coarse-grained density operator.
result: They prove that the system equilibrates within a timescale that scales polynomially with the system size, providing a rigorous derivation for macroscopic equilibration.
conclusion: This work establishes a rigorous foundation for equilibration timescales in free-fermion systems, contributing to the theoretical understanding of quantum thermalization.

title: Experimental Evidence For Strong Emergent Correlations Between Particles In A Switching Trap
authors: Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, and Grégory Schehr

We experimentally study a system of [MATH] two-dimensional Brownian particles, each confined in a harmonic trap with identical stiffness. The stiffness switches simultaneously between two values at random Poissonian times. This collective switching drives the system into a nonequilibrium stationary s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
