tldr: An experimental study of Brownian particles in a switching harmonic trap reveals strong emergent correlations in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how collective random switching drives correlations in many-particle systems out of equilibrium.
method: Trajectories of two Brownian particles in harmonic traps with randomly switching stiffness are recorded and analyzed.
result: Strong emergent correlations between particles are observed, characterized by a correlation function that diverges as the switching rate decreases.
conclusion: The system provides a tunable platform to study nonequilibrium correlations and may inform the thermodynamics of information processing in small systems.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of The Lindblad Master Equation And Its Nonlinear Extensions Via Quantum Trajectory Averaging
authors: Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, and Shu Chen

Since precisely controlling dissipation in realistic environments is challenging, digital simulation of the Lindblad master equation (LME) is of great significance for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems. However, achieving long-time simulations for complex systems with mul…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012436] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a digital quantum simulation method for Lindblad master equations and their nonlinear extensions using quantum trajectory averaging.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems is crucial for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics, but long-time simulations are challenging due to dissipation.
method: The method uses quantum trajectory averaging on a digital quantum computer, encoding the Lindblad equation as an ensemble of pure-state evolutions.
result: The approach can simulate both linear Lindblad equations and nonlinear extensions (e.g., mean-field master equations) with polynomial resource scaling.
conclusion: This work provides a practical digital simulation framework for open quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Precision-induced Irreversibility In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, And Diego Bautista Avilés
abstract:
Author(s): Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, and Diego Bautista Avilés

Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, yet finite dynamic range imposes a sharp operational limit on reversibility. We identify precision-induced irreversibility: Amplification, mode mixing (as warranted by non-normality), and a finite resolution floor—whether set by detector noise, e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies precision-induced irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems due to finite dynamic range, linking amplification and mode mixing to operational irreversibility.
motivation: Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, but practical limitations like finite resolution and noise impose a fundamental bound on reversibility, which is explored here.
method: The authors analyze non-Hermitian systems with amplification and non-normality, incorporating a finite resolution floor to model operational limits on reversibility.
result: They show that precision-induced irreversibility arises from the interplay of amplification, mode mixing, and finite dynamic range, providing a quantitative measure of irreversibility.
conclusion: The work establishes a thermodynamic-like irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems, relevant to information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Algorithms For Weakly Interacting Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Ryan L. Mann And Gabriel Waite
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan L. Mann and Gabriel Waite

We establish efficient algorithms for weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme for the thermal distribution over a classical spin spa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012432] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Provides efficient algorithms for approximating partition functions and sampling thermal distributions of weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature.
motivation: Computing thermodynamic properties of quantum systems is computationally hard in general; efficient algorithms are needed for physically relevant regimes.
method: Uses cluster expansion and quantum belief propagation to derive polynomial-time approximation schemes for partition functions and sampling.
result: Obtains a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling algorithm for thermal states.
conclusion: Weakly interacting quantum spin systems admit efficient classical algorithms for thermodynamic quantities, bridging quantum many-body physics and computational complexity.

title: Quantum Gate Broadcasting On Directed Acyclic Graphs
authors: Hiroki Sukeno And Tzu-Chieh Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Sukeno and Tzu-Chieh Wei

Using a generalized quantum gate teleportation protocol, copies of a gate encoding a known or unknown parameter can be sent to multiple receivers. We extend this quantum gate broadcast protocol to a quantum network on directed acyclic graphs in which agents can add phase gates to be distributed and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012611] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Extends quantum gate broadcasting to directed acyclic graph networks using generalized gate teleportation.
motivation: Quantum gate broadcasting allows a single gate to be applied to multiple receivers, which is useful for distributed quantum computing and quantum networks. Prior work focused on simple topologies; this paper generalizes to directed acyclic graphs.
method: Generalizes the quantum gate teleportation protocol to broadcast phase gates over directed acyclic graph networks, where agents can add gates to be distributed.
result: Provides a protocol for broadcasting gates on DAGs and analyzes its resource requirements and success probability.
conclusion: The protocol enables efficient distribution of quantum gates in complex network topologies, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Improving Shadow Estimation With Locally Optimal Dual Frames
authors: Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, And Daniel Cavalcanti
abstract:
Author(s): Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, and Daniel Cavalcanti

Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is a central challenge in quantum information science, yet practical implementations are fundamentally constrained by the limited number of measurement shots. In this work, we explore a variation of the classical shadows protocol in which the mea…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012428] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves classical shadow estimation by using locally optimal dual frames to reduce the number of measurement shots needed for accurate observable estimation.
motivation: Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is limited by the number of measurement shots; classical shadows provide a framework but can be inefficient for certain observables.
method: The authors propose a variation of the classical shadows protocol where the measurement basis is chosen adaptively using locally optimal dual frames, optimizing the estimation variance.
result: The locally optimal dual frames approach reduces the required number of measurement shots compared to standard classical shadows, especially for observables with low-rank structure.
conclusion: This work offers a practical improvement for quantum state estimation, making shadow estimation more efficient for near-term quantum devices.

title: Mutual Linearity In And Out Of Stationarity For Markov Jump Processes: A Trajectory-based Approach
authors: Jiming Zheng And Zhiyue Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiming Zheng and Zhiyue Lu

Nonequilibrium response theory is a fundamental framework for understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations. Recently, a mutual linearity has been discovered for Markov jump processes using linear algebra analysis. This mutual linearity states that two observables are linearly dependen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014126] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a mutual linearity between two observables in Markov jump processes, valid both in and out of stationarity, using a trajectory-based approach.
motivation: Understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations is fundamental; the authors aim to generalize response theory beyond linear response near equilibrium.
method: They employ a trajectory-based analysis of Markov jump processes, deriving a mutual linearity relation from the structure of the master equation without assuming detailed balance.
result: Two observables are shown to be linearly dependent even far from equilibrium, with the linear coefficient expressed in terms of trajectory statistics.
conclusion: The mutual linearity provides a new tool for analyzing non-equilibrium systems and may have implications for thermodynamic inference and fluctuation theorems.

title: Growth And Spreading Of Quantum Resources Under Random Circuit Dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, And Piotr Sierant
abstract:
Author(s): Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, and Piotr Sierant

Quantum many-body dynamics generate nonclassical correlations naturally described by quantum resource theories. Quantum magic resources (or nonstabilizerness) capture the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states, while coherence and fermionic non-Gaussianity measure departure from the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033062] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the growth and spreading of quantum magic resources under random circuit dynamics, providing analytical and numerical results for the generation of nonstabilizerness.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic (nonstabilizerness) spread in many-body systems is crucial for quantum computing and simulation, as it determines the onset of classical simulability.
method: The authors analyze random Clifford+T circuits and random Haar circuits, using measures of magic such as stabilizer Rényi entropy and mana, and study their dynamics via analytical calculations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that magic grows linearly in time and saturates to a volume-law scaling, with the growth rate depending on the density of T gates; they also characterize the spreading of magic correlations.
conclusion: The results provide a comprehensive picture of magic generation in random circuits, linking resource theory to many-body dynamics and offering insights into the complexity of quantum simulations.

title: Arbitrary Manipulation Of Nuclear Spins In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Fattah Sakuldee And Mehdi Abdi
abstract:
Author(s): Fattah Sakuldee and Mehdi Abdi

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to arbitrarily manipulate nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; the authors aim to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on these spins.
method: They design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radiofrequency pulses to control the nuclear spin via hyperfine interaction.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity arbitrary rotations of the nuclear spin, with fidelities exceeding 99% under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable path toward scalable quantum information processing using nuclear spins in hBN, leveraging existing defect center technology.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally characterizes coherent errors in a superconducting six-qubit network with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity, demonstrating high-fidelity gates and low error rates.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient quantum algorithms and error correction; however, coherent errors can limit performance. This work aims to characterize and mitigate such errors in a scalable superconducting processor.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with a bus resonator enabling all-to-all connectivity. They perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to measure gate fidelities and identify coherent error sources.
result: They achieve average single-qubit gate fidelities above 99.9% and two-qubit gate fidelities around 99.5%, with coherent errors dominated by residual ZZ interactions and control crosstalk.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity can be realized with high-fidelity gates, paving the way for more efficient quantum algorithms and error correction in superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Anharmonic Motion Of A Trapped Ion Under The Influence Of Different Drives In An Ion-nanomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Adrien Poindron And Stefan Willitsch
abstract:
Author(s): Adrien Poindron and Stefan Willitsch

Ions in traps hybridized with nanomechanical oscillators represent promising platforms for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating the classical and quantum motion of trapped particles. In a previous report [Weegen et al.,
tldr: This paper studies the anharmonic motion of a trapped ion coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator under various drives, analyzing classical and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Hybrid ion-nanomechanical systems are promising for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating trapped particle motion.
method: The authors model the system using a Hamiltonian that includes anharmonic trapping potentials and different drive schemes, solving the equations of motion analytically and numerically.
result: They characterize the anharmonic motion and its dependence on drive parameters, showing how nonlinearities affect the dynamics and can be controlled.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling ion motion in hybrid systems, relevant for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in many-body quantum systems, but experimental realization in a controlled platform has been challenging.
method: The authors engineer dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators and measure their relative phase.
result: They observe a fixed relative phase between the oscillators, indicating synchronization, accessible only through joint measurements.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a key quantum synchronization effect in a trapped-ion platform, opening avenues for studying collective quantum dynamics.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally realize and quantify a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable ultracold-atom platform.
method: Uses a processor of ultracold atoms to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system, benchmarking against classical simulations.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, meaning the task is beyond classical reach and the output is verifiable.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as viable platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantage in simulating complex quantum dynamics.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, including entropy accumulation and finite-size effects, to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, making high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.
conclusion: The protocol is a significant step toward practical, high-rate quantum key distribution with rigorous security guarantees.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, enabling higher-fidelity readout.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling scheme to suppress these transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, improving readout fidelity.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to higher-fidelity transmon readout, benefiting quantum computing platforms.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved impedance matching and nonlinearity to achieve broader bandwidth and higher saturation power.
result: The mixers demonstrate significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling efficient amplification and frequency conversion of quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing, particularly in superconducting qubit readout and quantum networking applications.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and higher key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV quantum networks, and related protocols.
result: CV quantum communication is now a mature field with record-breaking key rates and long-distance demonstrations, yet challenges remain in practical security and integration.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a promising and rapidly advancing area, with potential for widespread deployment in quantum networks.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their application to various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, though challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly accurate, aiding the design of better spin qubits, but further work is needed for complex environments.

title: Synchronized Aharonov-Bohm Motifs Via Engineered Dissipation
authors: Christopher W. Wächtler And Gloria Platero
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher W. Wächtler and Gloria Platero

The interplay between external gauge fields and lattice geometry can induce extreme localization dynamics through complete destructive interference. We show that combining this flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030405] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that combining flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin systems.
motivation: To achieve robust spin synchronization, which is important for quantum information processing, by exploiting the interplay between external gauge fields and dissipation.
method: The authors consider a rotationally symmetric spin system with an artificial gauge field (Aharonov-Bohm effect) and introduce engineered dissipation to stabilize synchronized states.
result: They demonstrate that the combination of flux-induced localization and dissipation yields robust spin synchronization, protected against certain perturbations.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation in the presence of gauge fields offers a viable route to realize and stabilize synchronized spin states, relevant for quantum technologies.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Calibration-Free Non-Markovian Noise Suppression
authors: Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, and Dawei Lu

Non-Markovian noise, arising from environmental memory effects, is the most general and challenging form of noise in quantum computing, and is typically difficult to characterize and suppress. Here, we analyze and experimentally demonstrate a non-Markovian noise suppression scheme inspired by quantu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030601] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a calibration-free scheme to suppress non-Markovian noise in quantum computing using a quantum autoencoder.
motivation: Non-Markovian noise is challenging to characterize and suppress, limiting quantum computing performance.
method: A quantum autoencoder is used to compress and filter out non-Markovian noise without requiring calibration or prior knowledge of the noise.
result: The scheme effectively suppresses non-Markovian noise in a nuclear magnetic resonance quantum processor, improving gate fidelity.
conclusion: Calibration-free non-Markovian noise suppression is experimentally feasible and enhances quantum computation robustness.

title: Engineering Quantum Noise Interference With Squeezed Vacuum In Dissipative Optomechanics
authors: Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, And Huaizhi Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, and Huaizhi Wu

Quantum noises impose limits on both backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators. Here, we demonstrate that for dissipative optomechanical systems in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable supp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise in dissipative optomechanical systems.
motivation: Quantum noise limits backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators; the authors aim to overcome these limits using squeezed light and Fano interference.
method: They theoretically analyze a dissipative optomechanical system in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, incorporating squeezed vacuum to engineer Fano interference and suppress quantum noise.
result: Broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise is achieved, improving the performance of optomechanical devices.
conclusion: Squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference is a viable technique for enhancing optomechanical sensing and cooling beyond standard quantum limits.

title: Resonant Blockade In Driven Quantum Oscillators
authors: B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

We investigate the emergence of synchronization blockade arising from the combined action of external driving and internal exchange interactions in quantum oscillators. The external drive indirectly influences the undriven mode through coupling to the driven mode, leading to a breakdown of limit cyc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012210] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies synchronization blockade in driven quantum oscillators due to external driving and internal exchange interactions.
motivation: Understanding synchronization in quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a model of coupled quantum oscillators with external driving and exchange interactions, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the external drive can induce a blockade of synchronization in the undriven mode, leading to a breakdown of limit cycle behavior.
conclusion: The results reveal new dynamical phenomena in quantum oscillators relevant to quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Linear-optical Schemes To Postselect High-dimensional Dicke States
authors: Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, And Seungbeom Chin
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, and Seungbeom Chin

Multipartite entanglement is an essential quantum resource for various distributed quantum applications. One promising method for preparing multipartite entanglement is to interfere independent photons at linear-optical interference setups. While heralding the successful interference and thereby the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013714] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes linear-optical schemes to postselect high-dimensional Dicke states, which are multipartite entangled states useful for quantum information applications.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is essential for distributed quantum applications, and high-dimensional Dicke states offer advantages but are challenging to prepare. Linear optics provides a scalable approach.
method: The authors design linear-optical interference setups that use postselection to herald the generation of high-dimensional Dicke states from independent photons.
result: The schemes achieve high success probabilities and fidelities for certain parameter regimes, demonstrating feasibility with current technology.
conclusion: The proposed linear-optical methods provide a practical route to generating high-dimensional Dicke states, which can benefit quantum communication and computation.

title: Entanglement Cohomology For Ghz And W States
authors: Christian Ferko And Keiichiro Furuya
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Ferko and Keiichiro Furuya

Entanglement cohomology assigns a graded cohomology ring to a multipartite pure state, providing homological invariants that are stable under local unitaries and characterize inequivalent patterns of entanglement. In this work we derive exact expressions for the dimensions of these cohomology groups…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012437] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces entanglement cohomology, a homological invariant for multipartite pure states, and computes its dimensions for GHZ and W states.
motivation: To develop new invariants that characterize inequivalent patterns of entanglement beyond traditional measures, stable under local unitary transformations.
method: Derives exact expressions for the dimensions of entanglement cohomology groups for GHZ and W states using algebraic topology and representation theory.
result: Provides explicit formulas for the cohomology dimensions, showing that GHZ and W states have distinct cohomological signatures.
conclusion: Entanglement cohomology offers a novel classification tool for multipartite entanglement, with potential applications in quantum information theory.

title: Spontaneous Breaking Of Time Translation Symmetry Via Spatially Inhomogeneous Many-body Interactions
authors: Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, and Xiangdong Zhang

Time crystals, with their intrinsic long-range temporal order and self-sustained oscillations, provide a unique platform for quantum applications that leverages long-lived coherence. We investigate the emergence of time-crystalline order in a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice featuring…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012612] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates spontaneous time translation symmetry breaking in a driven dissipative atomic lattice, realizing a time crystal phase.
motivation: Time crystals exhibit long-lived temporal order and self-sustained oscillations, offering a platform for quantum applications that leverage coherence.
method: The authors study a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice with spatially inhomogeneous many-body interactions, analyzing the emergence of time-crystalline order.
result: They show that spatially inhomogeneous interactions can stabilize a time crystal phase with robust oscillations.
conclusion: This work provides a new mechanism for realizing time crystals, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium phases of matter.

title: Dicke States For Two Accelerated Two-level Atoms
authors: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, And Marlan O. Scully
abstract:
Author(s): Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, and Marlan O. Scully

We study two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms moving in the right Rindler wedge and interacting with a massless scalar field. Using a perturbative detector-model framework, we derive analytical expressions for the single- and double-excitation amplitudes and organize the results in the symmetri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012813] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms interacting with a scalar field, deriving excitation amplitudes and analyzing Dicke states in the context of accelerated motion.
motivation: To understand how acceleration affects the collective behavior of atoms, particularly the symmetric and antisymmetric Dicke states, and to explore the interplay between acceleration and quantum correlations.
method: Using a perturbative detector-model framework, the authors derive analytical expressions for single- and double-excitation amplitudes for two accelerated atoms in the right Rindler wedge, organizing results in symmetrized and antisymmetrized forms.
result: Analytical expressions for excitation probabilities are obtained, showing how acceleration modifies the collective atomic dynamics and the role of Dicke states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-inertial quantum systems and their thermodynamic implications, relevant to quantum information in curved spacetimes.

title: Light-induced Quantum Self-trapping Of Vibrational Excitons In An Optical Cavity
authors: Vincent Pouthier And Saad Yalouz
abstract:
Author(s): Vincent Pouthier and Saad Yalouz

In an optical cavity, strong light-matter coupling between excitons and photons has been widely reported as a way to enhance energy delocalization through spatially extended polaritonic states. In contrast, leveraging cavity-mediated light-matter effects to promote the reciprocal phenomenon, namely,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013116] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that strong light-matter coupling in an optical cavity can induce quantum self-trapping of vibrational excitons, counteracting the usual delocalization effect.
motivation: To explore how cavity-mediated light-matter coupling can localize rather than delocalize excitons, potentially enabling new control over energy transport in molecular systems.
method: The authors model vibrational excitons coupled to a cavity mode using a Holstein-type Hamiltonian and solve the dynamics via a time-dependent variational approach with coherent states.
result: They find that for sufficiently strong coupling, the exciton becomes self-trapped, suppressing its motion and leading to a localized polaritonic state.
conclusion: Cavity-induced self-trapping offers a mechanism to control exciton mobility, with implications for quantum information processing and energy transfer in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Eigenstate Thermalization In The Weakly Interacting Holstein Polaron Model
authors: K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, And C. Sudheesh
abstract:
Author(s): K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, and C. Sudheesh

The origin of chaos in quantum systems remains a central challenge in many-body physics. Here, we use the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP) as a tool to investigate the transition from integrability to chaos in the one-dimensional Holstein polaron model. By combining exact diagonalization with an anal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014118] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses the adiabatic gauge potential to probe the transition from integrability to chaos in the Holstein polaron model, linking eigenstate thermalization to quantum chaos.
motivation: Understanding the origin of chaos in quantum many-body systems is a central challenge; the Holstein polaron model provides a testbed for studying thermalization.
method: The authors combine exact diagonalization with an analytical approach using the adiabatic gauge potential to diagnose chaos and integrability breaking.
result: They identify signatures of eigenstate thermalization and chaos in the weakly interacting regime of the Holstein polaron model.
conclusion: The adiabatic gauge potential is a useful tool for probing quantum chaos and thermalization in interacting many-body systems.

title: Inhomogeneous Mass Trap For Dark-state Polaritons In Atomic Media
authors: Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, And Wen-Te Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, and Wen-Te Liao

Spatially structured control fields generate an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency medium, enabling tunable bound states and coherent polariton dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032006] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an inhomogeneous mass trap for dark-state polaritons in atomic media using spatially structured control fields, enabling tunable bound states and coherent dynamics.
motivation: To achieve coherent control and trapping of dark-state polaritons, which are crucial for quantum information storage and processing in atomic ensembles.
method: The authors design spatially structured control fields in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency medium to create an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons.
result: They show that the trap potential can be tuned to support bound states and coherent polariton dynamics, with potential applications in quantum memory and information processing.
conclusion: The inhomogeneous mass trap provides a new tool for manipulating dark-state polaritons, advancing hybrid quantum systems that combine atomic media with light fields.

title: Verifiable End-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, And Anna Pappa
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, and Anna Pappa

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have emerged as promising candidates for solving complex optimization and machine learning tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, executing quantum operations remains challenging for small-scale users because of several hardware constraints, making it des…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033043] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithm (VQA) protocol that allows a client to outsource VQA computations to an untrusted quantum server while ensuring correctness.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum devices, but small-scale users lack access to powerful quantum hardware. Delegating computation to a quantum cloud raises trust issues, so a verifiable protocol is needed.
method: The protocol combines classical verification techniques with quantum operations, using trap qubits and measurement-based verification to detect malicious behavior by the server. It adapts existing verification methods to the VQA setting.
result: The protocol achieves end-to-end verifiability for VQAs with a polynomial overhead, and the authors prove its security against a dishonest server under standard assumptions.
conclusion: Verifiable delegated VQAs are feasible and can enable secure quantum cloud computing for near-term applications, bridging the gap between limited client hardware and powerful quantum servers.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code tailored for amplitude-damping noise and extends it to a family of codes correcting arbitrary orders of damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common decoherence mechanism in quantum systems, yet most quantum error-correcting codes are designed for generic errors. There is a need for noise-adapted codes that are more efficient for specific noise models.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors using a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery. They generalize this to a family of codes that correct up to any fixed order in the damping strength and derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code is the smallest possible for correcting single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes achieves higher rates than generic codes for this noise model.
conclusion: Noise-adapted quantum error correction can significantly reduce resource overhead for amplitude-damping noise, and the probabilistic framework provides a systematic way to construct such codes.

title: Sequential Analysis In A Continuous Spin-noise Quantum Sensor
authors: E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, And J. Calsamiglia
abstract:
Author(s): E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, and J. Calsamiglia

Many control and detection applications require real-time analysis of signals from sensors, in order to quickly and accurately act upon events revealed by the sensors. Such signal analysis benefits from statistical models of signal and sensor behavior. This creates a need for data analysis methods t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033038] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a sequential analysis framework for continuous spin-noise quantum sensors, enabling real-time detection of magnetic field changes with controlled error rates.
motivation: Real-time analysis of sensor signals is crucial for control and detection applications, but existing methods often lack statistical rigor or are not tailored to quantum sensors.
method: The authors propose a sequential hypothesis testing approach that processes the continuous output of a spin-noise sensor, using a statistical model of the sensor's noise and signal to update beliefs and make decisions as data arrives.
result: The method achieves fast and accurate detection of magnetic field changes, with provable bounds on false alarm and missed detection probabilities, demonstrated experimentally in a spin-noise magnetometer.
conclusion: Sequential analysis provides a principled and efficient way to extract information from continuous quantum sensors, with potential applications in magnetometry and other sensing tasks.

title: Fermionic Versus Spin Baths In Noninteracting Transport Models
authors: Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, And Brendon W. Lovett
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, and Brendon W. Lovett

We investigate how fermionic anticommutation shapes transport in a noninteracting resonant-level model where a single central site is coupled to an environment. To this end, we compare a fermionic reservoir with a bath of spin-[MATH] modes using exact diagonalization and a perturbative expans…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033030] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares fermionic and spin baths in a noninteracting resonant-level model, showing that fermionic anticommutation significantly affects transport properties.
motivation: Understanding how fermionic statistics influence transport in quantum systems is important for modeling realistic environments in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and a perturbative expansion to compare a fermionic reservoir with a spin bath in a noninteracting resonant-level model.
result: Fermionic anticommutation leads to qualitative differences in transport, such as suppression of current and different scaling with system size, compared to spin baths.
conclusion: Fermionic statistics must be accounted for in quantum transport models, as spin baths do not capture the correct physics of fermionic environments.

title: Rydberg Atoms For Electric Field Gradiometry
authors: Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, And Juan Polo
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, and Juan Polo

We propose a quantum sensor for electric fields based on networks of Rydberg atoms. The sensing mechanism exploits the strong dependence of the Rydberg blockade on the applied electric field near a Förster resonance. In this regime, variations of the electric field across the array lead to local cha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033010] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum sensor for electric fields using Rydberg atom networks, leveraging the Rydberg blockade near Förster resonance.
motivation: To develop a sensitive electric field gradiometer that exploits the strong dependence of Rydberg blockade on electric fields.
method: Uses networks of Rydberg atoms where the blockade radius changes with electric field near a Förster resonance, enabling local field variation detection.
result: Demonstrates that the sensor can measure electric field gradients with high sensitivity.
conclusion: Rydberg atom networks provide a promising platform for electric field gradiometry with potential applications in quantum sensing.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its efficient tensor-network representations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurately modeling open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging. The process tensor provides a unified framework to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics across various physical systems.
result: The paper shows that tensor-network process tensors can handle long memory times and large system sizes, making practical simulations feasible for problems in quantum thermodynamics, quantum optics, and condensed matter.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor-network methods, offers a powerful tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability to open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, enabling more complex protocols.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump dynamics.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and continuum limits that recover diffusion theory.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that treats both jump and diffusion processes on equal footing, enabling consistent analysis of pathwise observables.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying stochastic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium systems where both continuous and discrete dynamics occur.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensation and phase transitions in living cells can serve as a computational framework for processing high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: Cells must process complex, high-dimensional signals to respond to their environment, but traditional molecular signaling pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, nonlinear mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors draw analogies between phase separation in biomolecular condensates and computational processes such as classification, sensing, and decision-making, supported by theoretical arguments and examples from cell biology.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to perform computations like threshold detection, noise filtering, and multiplexing, effectively acting as physical computers.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a powerful, physically-grounded paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for understanding biological computation and designing synthetic systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage to highly excited states.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing leakage errors in superconducting qubits.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize the excited-state dynamics of transmon qubits, identifying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They observe and quantify the ionization process, showing how qubits escape the computational subspace through specific resonance conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, which can inform better readout and error mitigation strategies for superconducting quantum processors.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the atom's small mass for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the unique properties of helium-3 atoms, such as their small mass and metastable states, for quantum information processing and simulation applications.
method: The authors analyze the advantages of helium-3 in optical tweezer arrays, focusing on continuous-variable quantum computing and tunable hopping for quantum simulation of materials.
result: Helium-3 atoms enable stronger tunneling and interaction strengths compared to other atomic species, making them suitable for continuous-variable quantum computing and simulating Hubbard models with tunable parameters.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays offer a promising platform for quantum science, particularly in continuous-variable computing and quantum simulation of strongly correlated materials.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but their two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by short Rydberg lifetimes due to blackbody radiation.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around the atom array, thereby suppressing blackbody-induced transitions and extending Rydberg state lifetimes.
result: They demonstrate significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes in a cryogenic environment, which directly reduces the dominant relaxation error in Rydberg-mediated gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is an effective strategy to improve gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers, bringing them closer to fault-tolerant thresholds.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks can preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning sequentially; quantum neural networks may offer intrinsic advantages due to their parameter structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks theoretically and empirically, showing that overparameterization does not lead to loss of plasticity.
result: Quantum neural networks maintain the ability to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones, even as the number of parameters grows.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks provide a promising platform for continual learning, with potential applications in adaptive quantum information processing.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics, which are computationally expensive, using a photonic platform that is highly configurable.
method: Decomposes a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling simulation algorithms on a photonic chip.
result: Demonstrates a configurable photonic simulator that can efficiently execute quantum field dynamics simulations.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical and scalable approach to studying quantum field theories.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Improving displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Spin-dependent squeezing offers a path to surpass standard quantum limits.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a trapped-ion scheme where spin-dependent forces generate squeezed states of motion, then use these states for displacement sensing.
result: They show that spin-dependent squeezed states achieve the Heisenberg limit for displacement estimation, outperforming coherent and squeezed vacuum states.
conclusion: Trapped-ion platforms with spin-dependent squeezing are a promising route for optimal quantum sensing, with potential applications in force and field detection.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation without exhaustive sampling.
result: The framework successfully identifies the number and properties of spin baths in simulated and experimental NV center data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient, scalable tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with applications to hybrid quantum systems and quantum sensing.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but efficient loading and imaging with low loss remain challenging. EIT offers a solution for nondestructive detection and continuous loading.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve nondestructive imaging of atom arrays, and use this technique to continuously load atoms into the array while maintaining high fidelity.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, with reduced atom loss compared to conventional methods, enabled by EIT in a finite magnetic field.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provides a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation, improving array preparation and readout.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for fault-tolerant quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path toward implementing error correction in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating a compact and scalable device for quantum security.
motivation: Quantum random number generation with self-testing provides provable security, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. This work aims to miniaturize such a system on a photonic chip.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for self-testing quantum randomness expansion, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and control logic.
result: The chip successfully generates random numbers with self-testing guarantees, achieving high generation rates and demonstrating the feasibility of on-chip quantum randomness expansion.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, miniaturized quantum security devices that can be mass-produced, advancing the deployment of quantum networks and cryptography.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in semiconductor qubit devices, revealing new features in the noise spectrum.
conclusion: This technique provides a powerful tool for noise characterization in qubit platforms, aiding in the development of more coherent quantum devices.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve. This work explores whether collective effects in an ensemble can enhance photon blockade.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission as the number of emitters increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a viable route to achieve strong photon blockade without demanding single-emitter parameters, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central task in machine computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum singular value transformation, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a structured overview of the state of the art, highlighting key improvements in query complexity, precision, and applicability to sparse and dense matrices.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging; the survey identifies open problems and future directions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The paper systematically compares different methods, highlighting their commonalities and differences, and provides guidance for choosing appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework and comparative analysis help researchers navigate the diverse landscape of non-Markovian simulation methods, advancing both theoretical understanding and practical applications.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum algorithms, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can improve efficiency in quantum computing, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum information processing, warranting further theoretical and experimental exploration.

title: Non-Markovian Quantum Mpemba Effect In Strongly Correlated Quantum Dots
authors: Yuandong Wang And Jianhua Wei
abstract: Harnessing non-Markovian effects has emerged as a resource for quantum control, where a structured environment can act as a quantum memory. We investigate the quench dynamics from specific initial states to equilibrium steady states in strongly correlated quantum dot systems. The distance between quantum states is quantified using the Bures metric, which endows the space of reduced density matrices with a Riemannian geometric structure. Using the numerically exact hierarchical equations of motion method, we demonstrate a quantum Mpemba effect (QME) arising from non-Markovianity. Unlike previous studies centered on non-interacting limits, we reveal a distinct non-Markovian QME uniquely driven by the initial-state-dependent formation of the many-body Kondo resonance. Furthermore, by tracking the dynamical evolution in the generalized Bloch parameter space, we uncover an intrinsic QME. This trajectory-dependent analysis provides a rigorous geometric perspective on the circuitous relaxation pathways driven by Kondo correlations. Our results underscore the critical role of memory effects in quantum quench dynamics and suggest new pathways for controlling anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a non-Markovian quantum Mpemba effect in strongly correlated quantum dots, driven by Kondo correlations and memory effects.
