motivation: Understanding anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems is important for quantum control; the quantum Mpemba effect offers a way to harness non-Markovianity.
method: The authors use the numerically exact hierarchical equations of motion method to simulate quench dynamics and quantify state distance via the Bures metric.
result: They reveal a distinct non-Markovian QME uniquely driven by initial-state-dependent formation of the many-body Kondo resonance, and uncover an intrinsic QME via geometric analysis in Bloch parameter space.
conclusion: Memory effects play a critical role in quantum quench dynamics, and the findings suggest new pathways for controlling anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems.

title: Saturation Attack Of The Microwave-propagated Continuous Variable Quantum Key Distribution In Open Air
authors: Wenqi Peng, Xuan Li, Yongxin Feng, Xiu-Bo Chen And Ying Guo
abstract: Continuous variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD) can achieve the secure communication between two distant legitimate users. The microwave CVQKD exhibits stronger robustness than the optical CVQKD in transmitting quantum signals and accordingly has broad application prospects in quantum networks. Although the microwave CVQKD does not rely on the traditional optical fibers to transmit quantum signals, its practical security is still vulnerable to saturation attacks. In view of this security vulnerability, we generalize saturation attacks to microwave CVQKD and clarify the impact of saturation attacks on the parameter estimation of microwave systems. Two saturation attack schemes are further compared, one based on displacement control alone and the other on joint displacement and gain control. To mitigate the negative impacts caused by this attack, we propose a countermeasure based on the quantum nearest neighbor algorithm, which can detect saturation attacks by measuring unknown quantum states. In addition, the influence of microwave antennas on the security of the communication system is assessed, confirming that antenna gain plays a key role in determining both the secret key rate and the maximum transmission distance.
tldr: This paper generalizes saturation attacks to microwave CVQKD and proposes a countermeasure using quantum nearest neighbor algorithm.
motivation: Microwave CVQKD offers robust quantum signal transmission but is vulnerable to saturation attacks; the paper aims to analyze and mitigate this security threat.
method: The authors model two saturation attack schemes (displacement control alone vs. joint displacement and gain control) and propose a detection countermeasure based on quantum nearest neighbor algorithm.
result: The analysis shows that antenna gain significantly impacts secret key rate and maximum transmission distance; the proposed countermeasure can detect saturation attacks.
conclusion: Saturation attacks pose a practical security risk to microwave CVQKD, but can be mitigated with appropriate detection methods, highlighting the importance of antenna design.

title: Capturing An Electron In The Virtual State
authors: Alok Nath Singh, Bibek Bhandari, Rafael Sánchez And Andrew N Jordan
abstract: We address a foundational question in quantum mechanics: can a particle be directly found in a classically-forbidden virtual state? We instantiate this conceptual question by investigating the traversal of electrons through a tunnel barrier, which we define in a triple quantum dot system where the occupation of the central dot is energetically avoided. The motivation behind this setup is to answer whether the central dot is occupied or not during a virtual transition when it is being explicitly monitored. We investigate this problem in two different limits of continuous measurements: the stochastic quantum diffusion and the quantum jump. We find that, even though individual trajectories differ considerably across these limits, measuring leads to a higher occupation in the central dot on average. We also find that a suitably strong measurement can significantly boost the tunneling current—an effect we call measurement-assisted tunneling. Our results demonstrate that the act of observation fundamentally reshapes tunneling dynamics, resolving the seeming paradox of detecting a particle in a classically forbidden region: weak measurements partially localize the particle, while strong measurements enforce a discontinuous either/or detection or no detection outcome.
tldr: This paper investigates whether an electron can be detected in a classically forbidden virtual state by monitoring a triple quantum dot system, revealing measurement-assisted tunneling.
motivation: To resolve the paradox of detecting a particle in a virtual state and understand how continuous measurement reshapes tunneling dynamics.
method: The authors model a triple quantum dot with energetically avoided central dot occupation and analyze two continuous measurement limits: stochastic quantum diffusion and quantum jumps.
result: Measurements increase average occupation of the central dot, and strong measurement can boost tunneling current, an effect called measurement-assisted tunneling.
conclusion: The act of observation fundamentally alters tunneling, with weak measurements partially localizing the particle and strong measurements enforcing discontinuous detection outcomes.

title: Quantum Wiener Architecture For Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Alessio Benavoli And Felix C. Binder
abstract:
Author(s): Alessio Benavoli and Felix C. Binder

This work focuses on quantum reservoir computing and, in particular, on quantum Wiener architectures (qWiener), consisting of quantum linear dynamic networks with weak continuous measurements and classical nonlinear static readouts. We provide the first rigorous proof that qWiener systems retain the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012433] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides the first rigorous proof that quantum Wiener systems, consisting of linear quantum dynamics with weak measurements and classical nonlinear readouts, can approximate any fading memory nonlinear system, establishing a theoretical foundation for quantum reservoir computing.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is a promising paradigm for temporal information processing, but lacks rigorous theoretical guarantees. The authors aim to provide a solid mathematical foundation for QRC using the Wiener architecture.
method: The authors define quantum Wiener systems as linear quantum networks with weak continuous measurements and classical nonlinear readouts. They prove that such systems are universal approximators for fading memory nonlinear systems using the theory of Volterra series and the Stone-Weierstrass theorem.
result: They show that any fading memory nonlinear system can be approximated arbitrarily well by a quantum Wiener system, and provide explicit bounds on the approximation error in terms of the number of quantum nodes and measurement strength.
conclusion: Quantum Wiener systems offer a theoretically grounded and practically viable approach to quantum reservoir computing, with potential advantages in computational power and energy efficiency over classical reservoirs.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Simulating quantum circuits classically is hard, but for small subregions of the landscape, classical surrogates may be efficient and useful for optimization or understanding.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a patch of the expectation landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical post-processing, likely using tensor networks or other classical approximations.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values for nearby points in the landscape with significantly less quantum resource usage than full simulation.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical hybrid quantum-classical strategy for exploring quantum landscapes, potentially aiding in variational algorithms or quantum circuit optimization.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation framework that uses a moment-matching technique to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger Hilbert space, realized via a tight-binding lattice.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical and efficient way to simulate nonunitary processes on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that operate in frequency space to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables, leveraging the periodic structure of Floquet systems.
result: The method accurately learns Floquet Hamiltonians and predicts observable dynamics and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Self-dual Bivariate Bicycle Codes With Transversal Clifford Gates
authors: Zijian Liang
Yu-An Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper constructs a family of self-dual bivariate bicycle codes that admit transversal Clifford gates, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Transversal gates are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but no known code family simultaneously has high rate, high distance, and a universal transversal gate set. This work aims to find codes with transversal Clifford gates.
method: The authors generalize the bivariate bicycle code construction to self-dual codes using a specific polynomial condition, and prove that these codes support transversal Hadamard, phase, and CNOT gates.
result: They present explicit code families with parameters [[2d^2, 2, d]] for odd d, achieving transversal Clifford gates and high encoding rate.
conclusion: Self-dual bivariate bicycle codes provide a promising platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation with transversal Clifford gates, though they do not achieve universality without additional non-Clifford resources.

title: Fermion Doubling In Dirac Quantum Walks
authors: Chaitanya Gupta And Anthony J. Short
abstract:
Author(s): Chaitanya Gupta and Anthony J. Short

We consider discrete spacetime models known as quantum walks, which can be used to simulate Dirac particles. In particular, we look at fermion doubling in these models, in which high-momentum states yield additional low-energy solutions which behave like Dirac particles. The presence of doublers car…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012208] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fermion doubling in discrete-time quantum walks, showing that doublers appear due to the chirality of the walk and can be eliminated by breaking chirality.
motivation: Fermion doubling is a known issue in lattice field theory, and understanding its manifestation in quantum walks is important for using quantum walks as simulators of relativistic particles.
method: The authors analyze the dispersion relation of Dirac quantum walks on a one-dimensional lattice, identifying conditions for doublers and proposing a non-chiral walk that avoids them.
result: They prove that any chiral quantum walk on a regular lattice exhibits fermion doubling, and demonstrate a non-chiral walk that is free of doublers.
conclusion: Fermion doubling in quantum walks is a consequence of chirality, and can be avoided by breaking chirality, enabling more accurate quantum simulations of Dirac particles.

title: Non-Markovian Renormalization Of Optomechanical Exceptional Points
authors: Aritra Ghosh And M. Bhattacharya
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Ghosh and M. Bhattacharya

We investigate how non-Markovian mechanical dissipation affects exceptional points in linearized optomechanical systems with red-sideband drive. For a chosen non-Ohmic mechanical bath, we derive analytical conditions for the memory-renormalized exceptional point by employing a pseudomode mapping, th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013516] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how non-Markovian mechanical dissipation renormalizes exceptional points in optomechanical systems.
motivation: Exceptional points in optomechanics are sensitive to dissipation; understanding non-Markovian effects is important for controlling these systems.
method: The authors use a pseudomode mapping to derive analytical conditions for memory-renormalized exceptional points under non-Ohmic mechanical baths.
result: They find that non-Markovian dissipation shifts the exceptional point and modifies the system's dynamics compared to Markovian approximations.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects must be accounted for in optomechanical systems to accurately predict exceptional point behavior.

title: Gaussian Tomography For Cold-atom Simulators
authors: Matthew Kiser, Max Mcginley, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Kiser, Max McGinley, and Daniel Malz

A limitation of analog quantum simulators based on cold atoms in optical lattices is that readout is typically limited to observables diagonal in the charge basis, i.e., densities and density correlation functions. To overcome this limitation, we propose experiment-friendly schemes to measure charge…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013311] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes experiment-friendly Gaussian tomography schemes for cold-atom quantum simulators to measure non-diagonal observables.
motivation: Analog quantum simulators based on cold atoms in optical lattices are limited to measuring only diagonal observables (densities and density correlations), restricting their utility for studying quantum information and many-body physics.
method: The authors design Gaussian tomography protocols that exploit the Gaussian nature of the quantum states produced by the simulator, enabling efficient reconstruction of the full covariance matrix via simple measurements.
result: The proposed schemes allow measurement of off-diagonal observables such as currents and entanglement witnesses, significantly expanding the readout capabilities of cold-atom simulators.
conclusion: Gaussian tomography provides a practical path to overcome readout limitations in cold-atom simulators, enabling access to a broader class of observables relevant to quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Randomly Measured Quantum Particles And Thermal Noise
authors: Victor Gurarie
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Gurarie

We consider the motion of a quantum particle whose position is measured in random places at random moments in time. We contrast this motion with the motion of a quantum particle in a potential which varies randomly in space and in time, which could also be thought of as (possibly thermal) noise. We …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012205] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the motion of a quantum particle under random position measurements and compares it to motion in a random potential (thermal noise).
motivation: To understand the effect of random measurements on quantum dynamics and contrast it with classical thermal noise.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a quantum particle subjected to random position measurements at random times, and comparison with a particle in a spatiotemporally random potential.
result: The random measurement process leads to diffusive behavior similar to thermal noise, but with distinct features.
conclusion: Random measurements can mimic thermal noise, but the underlying mechanisms differ, providing insight into measurement-induced dynamics.

title: Quantum Complexity In Rule-based Constrained Many-body Models: Scars, Fragmentation, And Chaos
authors: Arkaprava Sil And Sudipto Singha Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Arkaprava Sil and Sudipto Singha Roy

Kinetic constraints in quantum many-body systems strongly restrict the accessible Hilbert space, giving rise to highly nontrivial dynamical behavior. In recent years, such systems have attracted growing interest as they provide insight into mechanisms of thermalization and into regimes where thermal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024312] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars, Hilbert space fragmentation, and chaos in constrained models, linking them to thermalization and complexity.
motivation: Understanding how kinetic constraints lead to non-thermal behavior and complex dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
method: Analyzes rule-based constrained models using exact diagonalization and entanglement measures to characterize scars, fragmentation, and chaos.
result: Identifies conditions for quantum many-body scars and fragmentation, and relates them to quantum complexity measures.
conclusion: Constrained many-body models exhibit rich dynamical phases that challenge thermalization, with implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement Dynamics In Minimal Kitaev Chains
authors: Vimalesh Kumar Vimal And Jorge Cayao
abstract:
Author(s): Vimalesh Kumar Vimal and Jorge Cayao

Minimal Kitaev chains host Majorana quasiparticles, which, although not topologically protected, exhibit spatial nonlocality and hence are expected to be useful for quantum information tasks. In this work, we consider two- and three-site Kitaev chains and investigate the dynamics of bipartite and mu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034308] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in minimal Kitaev chains with two and three sites, focusing on Majorana quasiparticles.
motivation: Minimal Kitaev chains host Majorana quasiparticles with spatial nonlocality, which are expected to be useful for quantum information tasks, motivating the study of their entanglement dynamics.
method: The authors consider two- and three-site Kitaev chains and investigate the dynamics of bipartite and multipartite entanglement using numerical simulations.
result: The paper characterizes how entanglement evolves in these minimal systems, revealing features related to Majorana nonlocality.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement properties of minimal Kitaev chains, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core quantum information topics like entanglement theory or quantum cryptography.

title: Caloric Phenomena And Stirling-cycle Performance In Heisenberg-Kitaev Magnon Systems
authors: Bastian Castorene, Martin Hve Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, And Patricio Vargas
abstract:
Author(s): Bastian Castorene, Martin HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, and Patricio Vargas

We investigate the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg–Kitaev magnonic medium with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions, finding symmetric caloric responses and efficiency.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of quantum magnetic systems as working media in heat engines.
method: Linear spin-wave theory is used to compute the magnon spectrum and caloric properties, then the Stirling cycle efficiency is evaluated.
result: DM interactions preserve spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency.
conclusion: The Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions can serve as a working medium for Stirling cycles with symmetric performance.

title: Generic Signatures Of non-Markovian Dynamics In The Presence Of A Magnetic Field
authors: Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, And Bidhan Chandra Bag
abstract:
Author(s): Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, and Bidhan Chandra Bag

In this paper, we have presented the three-dimensional dynamics in the velocity space of a Brownian particle coupled to a non-Markovian thermal bath in the presence of a magnetic field (MF), as well as external deterministic and stochastic force fields. The directions of the MF and the deterministic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014121] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of a Brownian particle in a magnetic field, focusing on velocity-space signatures.
motivation: Understanding non-Markovian effects in the presence of a magnetic field is important for modeling realistic open quantum systems.
method: The authors derive three-dimensional Langevin equations for a Brownian particle coupled to a non-Markovian thermal bath with a magnetic field, and analyze the velocity correlation functions and mean squared displacement.
result: They find that the magnetic field induces oscillatory behavior in the velocity correlations and modifies the non-Markovian signatures, such as the appearance of negative values in the velocity autocorrelation function.
conclusion: The presence of a magnetic field can be used to control or detect non-Markovianity in Brownian motion, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Access-limited Equilibration And Observable-dependent Relaxation In Lattice-gas Systems
authors: Marvin A. Albao
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin A. Albao

We investigate equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted coupling to a particle reservoir. Using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, we isolate the role of reservoir-access geometry by comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region w…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014124] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted reservoir access, using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand how the geometry of reservoir coupling affects relaxation and equilibration in many-body systems, which is relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of a lattice-gas model comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region.
result: The paper isolates the role of reservoir-access geometry on equilibration dynamics, showing observable-dependent relaxation.
conclusion: The geometry of reservoir coupling significantly influences equilibration, but the work is a classical statistical mechanics study without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Covariant Formulation Of The Berry Connection In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ievgen I. Arkhipov
abstract:
Author(s): Ievgen I. Arkhipov

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit spectral and topological phenomena absent in Hermitian physics; however, their geometric characterization remains subtle due to the intrinsic ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. Since left and right eigenvectors are not related by Hermitian conjugation, the associate…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033037] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant formulation of the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, addressing the ambiguity in biorthogonal eigenspaces.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique spectral and topological phenomena, but their geometric characterization is subtle due to the lack of Hermitian conjugation between left and right eigenvectors.
method: The authors propose a covariant approach to define the Berry connection and curvature that is independent of the choice of biorthogonal basis, using a gauge-invariant formalism.
result: They derive explicit expressions for the covariant Berry connection and show that it reduces to the standard Hermitian result in the appropriate limit, while capturing non-Hermitian topological features.
conclusion: The covariant formulation provides a consistent geometric framework for non-Hermitian systems, enabling further study of topological phases in open quantum systems.

title: Learning Complexity Gradually In Quantum Machine Learning Models
authors: Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, And Carlos Bravo-Prieto
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, and Carlos Bravo-Prieto

Quantum machine learning is an emergent field that continues to draw significant interest for its potential to offer improvements over classical algorithms in certain areas. However, training quantum models remains a challenging task, largely because of the difficulty in establishing an effective in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033006] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to gradually increase the complexity of quantum machine learning models during training to improve performance and avoid barren plateaus.
motivation: Training quantum machine learning models is challenging due to issues like barren plateaus and difficulty in finding effective initializations.
method: The authors introduce a training scheme where the expressivity of the quantum model is progressively increased, starting from a simpler model and adding complexity as training proceeds.
result: The gradual complexity approach leads to better convergence and final performance compared to training the full model from the start, and helps mitigate barren plateaus.
conclusion: Gradually increasing model complexity is a promising strategy for training quantum machine learning models, making them more practical.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces new control parameters for generating non-Gaussian quantum states in optical systems, enabling scalable and high-success-rate state generation.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing, but their generation suffers from low success rates. The authors aim to overcome this by introducing systematic optimization parameters.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank, which characterize the non-Gaussianity of quantum states, and develop a method to optimize these parameters for state generation.
result: The new control parameters allow for orders-of-magnitude increase in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states, demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable framework for generating non-Gaussian states, which is crucial for advancing optical quantum computing and quantum networks.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, identifying depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques from statistical physics and random matrix theory, deriving universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of circuit depth and noise strength.
result: They find that anticoncentration exhibits three regimes: a noise-free regime, a universal regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially with depth, and a deep-circuit regime where it saturates to a constant. The universal regime is independent of circuit architecture.
conclusion: The results provide a comprehensive understanding of anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, with implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and the design of random circuit benchmarks.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods struggle with large multiqubit unitaries. The authors aim to extend the reach of stabilizer-based simulation by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for larger systems, building on the Gottesman-Knill theorem and Clifford circuit properties.
result: The proposed methods enable classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, demonstrating significant speedups for certain classes of circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for simulating near-Clifford circuits, which are relevant to quantum advantage experiments and error correction.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear definitions and quantitative measures of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical frameworks to define Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, and introduce measures of robustness and locality based on topological invariants and entanglement properties.
result: They provide quantitative criteria for when Majorana bound states are well-defined and protected, and show how interactions affect their robustness and non-Abelian braiding potential.
conclusion: The work offers a rigorous foundation for identifying and characterizing Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward topological qubits.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Harvesting For Two Rotating Atoms In A Cylindrical Cavity
authors: Hong-Tao Zheng, Xiang-Fa Zhou, Guang-Can Guo And Zheng-Wei Zhou
abstract: We study the entanglement dynamics of two rotating atoms (with two internal levels and ) in a cylindrical cavity, which interact with a massless scalar field in vacuum satisfying the Dirichlet boundary condition. Our analysis demonstrates that it is possible to obtain the steady-state entanglement under two types of resonant conditions. For two identical atoms with the same world-line, the system reduces to the usual dissipative Dicke model at the first resonant condition where and are the energy splitting and the angular velocity of the th atom, and is the Lorentz factor. The entangled steady-state takes the form where and are constant, which is consistent with the previous study (see 2022 Phys. Rev. D 106 105028). For two atoms with different world-lines, the system suffers from a significant mixed joint dissipation process at the second resonant condition , and reaches an entangled steady-state as . Moreover, with the help of the cavity, we can obtain a much higher concurrence in the final states by changing the relative ratio of the two orbital radii. Our work thus provides a more effective way for the extraction of steady-state entanglement from the vacuum via the analogue Unruh effect for two rotating atoms in a cylindrical cavity.
tldr: This paper studies steady-state entanglement harvesting from vacuum for two rotating atoms in a cylindrical cavity, using the analogue Unruh effect.
motivation: To understand how motion and boundary conditions affect entanglement extraction from quantum vacuum, and to achieve steady-state entanglement for practical quantum information tasks.
method: The authors model two two-level atoms rotating in a cylindrical cavity with Dirichlet boundary conditions, interacting with a massless scalar field. They derive master equations and analyze resonant conditions for steady-state entanglement.
result: Steady-state entanglement is obtained under two resonant conditions, with higher concurrence achievable by tuning orbital radii. The system reduces to a dissipative Dicke model for identical atoms.
conclusion: The work provides an effective method for extracting steady-state entanglement from vacuum via the Unruh effect, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Generating Logical Magic States With The Aid Of non-Abelian Topological Order
authors: Sheng-Jie Huang
Yanzhu Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate logical magic states using non-Abelian topological order, leveraging anyonic quasiparticles for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computation, but their generation is challenging. Topological systems offer inherent fault tolerance, and non-Abelian anyons may provide a natural resource for magic states.
method: The authors design a protocol using non-Abelian topological order, specifically Ising anyons, to create logical magic states through braiding and measurement operations.
result: They demonstrate that logical magic states can be generated with high fidelity using topological operations, and analyze the resource overhead and error thresholds.
conclusion: Non-Abelian topological order provides a viable platform for generating magic states, potentially reducing the overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Training The Classification Capability Of Large-scale Quantum Cellular Automata
authors: Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, and Igor Lesanovsky

In the vicinity of a phase transition ergodicity can be broken. title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.

tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlation physics and optical control.

method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoping, thermalization, and emergence of metastable orders (superconducting, magnetic, etc.) are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate correlated materials, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Green’s Function Methods For Computing Supercurrents In Josephson Junctions
authors: Eduardo R Mucciolo, Jouko Nieminen, Xiao Xiao, Wei-Chi Chiu, Michael N Leuenberger And Arun Bansil
abstract: Interest in Josephson junctions (JJs) has increased rapidly in recent years not only because of their use in qubits and other quantum devices but also due to the unique physics supported by the JJs. The advent of various novel quantum materials for both the barrier region and the superconducting leads has led to the possibility of adding new functionalities to the JJs. Thus, there is a growing need for accurate modeling of the JJs and related systems to enable their predictive control and atomistic level understanding. This review presents an in-depth discussion of a Green’s-function-based formalism for computing supercurrents in JJs. The formulation is tailored for large-scale atomistic simulations and encompasses both dc and ac supercurrents. We hope that this review will provide a timely and comprehensive reference for researchers as well as beginning practitioners interested in Green’s-function-based methods to model supercurrents in JJs.
tldr: A review of Green's function methods for computing supercurrents in Josephson junctions, focusing on large-scale atomistic simulations.
motivation: Josephson junctions are key components in qubits and quantum devices, and accurate modeling is needed for predictive control and atomistic understanding.
method: The paper presents a Green's-function-based formalism tailored for large-scale atomistic simulations to compute both dc and ac supercurrents.
result: The formalism enables accurate modeling of supercurrents in Josephson junctions with novel quantum materials.
conclusion: This review provides a comprehensive reference for researchers interested in Green's-function-based modeling of supercurrents in Josephson junctions.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to unify dynamical evolution via space-time duality.
method: The review focuses on discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and relating to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It provides a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems through the lens of quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful framework for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics.

abstract:

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to model neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to experimental recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover reproducible behaviors and provide predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics offers a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment.

motivation: Accurate measurement of laser frequency variations is crucial for applications like LiDAR and spectroscopy. Existing methods are limited in speed or precision.
method: Two electro-optic frequency combs with slightly different repetition rates are generated on a lithium niobate chip. The frequency-modulated laser is beat against these combs, and the beat signals are analyzed to extract the instantaneous frequency.
result: The technique achieves stable and high-precision tracking of frequency variations, enabling 3D scene ranging with improved accuracy.
conclusion: Integrated electro-optic combs provide a compact and effective solution for dynamic laser frequency measurement, with potential for practical ranging systems.

title: Emergence Of Fermi-liquid And Bcs Physics In Overdoped Cuprates
authors: B. J. Ramshaw
Steven A. Kivelson
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that observed behaviors in overdoped cuprates can be explained by substitutional disorder in a d-wave superconductor, rather than requiring non-Fermi-liquid physics.
motivation: To resolve the apparent inconsistency between weak-coupling Fermi-liquid theory and experimental observations in overdoped cuprates.
method: The authors present a perspective based on theoretical arguments and analysis of substitutional disorder effects in d-wave superconductors.
result: They propose that in the disorder-free limit, a weak-coupling Fermi-liquid description is possible, and disorder explains the observed deviations.
conclusion: Substitutional disorder is key to understanding overdoped cuprate behavior, and a Fermi-liquid-based BCS approach is viable without disorder.

title: Universities Need Transparent Quantum Hardware
authors: Alex Krasnok
Arif Sarwat
William Anderson Jr.
Andres Gil
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that universities should procure transparent quantum hardware for educational purposes rather than relying solely on cloud access.
motivation: The authors believe that students need hands-on experience with quantum hardware to understand the transition from ideal circuits to physical measurements.
method: The paper presents a perspective based on educational needs and the limitations of cloud-based quantum computing access.
result: It advocates for universities to invest in teachable quantum systems that allow students to interact with the hardware directly.
conclusion: Universities should prioritize educational transparency over high-performance but opaque quantum machines.

title: Non-idealities In Artificial Synapses
authors: Shafin Bin Hamid
Jean Anne C. Incorvia
Samuel Liu
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews non-idealities in artificial synapses based on non-volatile memory for neuromorphic computing.
motivation: Non-ideal effects in artificial synapses can limit neuromorphic system performance, so understanding their origins and mitigation is important.
method: The paper reviews various non-idealities, their physical origins, mitigation strategies, and opportunities to exploit them for new computing functionalities.
result: It categorizes non-idealities and discusses both challenges and potential benefits.
conclusion: Non-idealities in artificial synapses can be mitigated or exploited to enhance neuromorphic computing.

title: Ultrahigh Spatiotemporal Resolution Terahertz Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy
authors: Jiayu Xu
Yunpeng Xia
Qiuyan Lin
Shijing Tan
Bing Wang
Jia-Xin Yin
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy for ultrafast electron dynamics and molecular motions.
motivation: To achieve ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution for studying ultrafast phenomena in quantum materials.
method: Integrates picosecond terahertz pulses with scanning tunnelling microscopy.
result: Enables detailed analysis of electron dynamics and molecular motions at atomic resolution.
conclusion: The technique offers insights into ultrafast phenomena and potential advances in quantum materials and technologies.

title: Flow Matching For Reaction Pathway Generation
authors: Ping Tuo
Jiale Chen
Ju Li
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 17 July 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a flow-matching framework for generating reaction pathways in chemistry, focusing on molecular reaction products and transition states.
motivation: Efficient discovery of reaction pathways is crucial for chemistry and materials science, but traditional methods are computationally expensive.
method: The authors propose MolGEN, an optimal transport flow-matching model that generates reaction products and transition states by learning a continuous transformation between reactant and product distributions.
result: The framework enables faster reaction-pathway discovery and identifies lower-energy routes compared to existing methods.
conclusion: Flow matching provides a promising generative approach for reaction pathway generation, with potential applications in computational chemistry.

title: Interference And Short-Range Correlation In Fermionic Hubbard Gases
authors: Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:

The interference patterns of ultracold atoms, observed after ballistic expansion from optical lattices, encode essential information about strongly correlated lattice systems, including phase coherence and nonlocal correlations. While the interference of lattice bosons has been extensively investiga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033401] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interference patterns and short-range correlations in fermionic Hubbard gases after ballistic expansion from optical lattices.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated lattice systems is important, and interference patterns provide information about phase coherence and nonlocal correlations.
method: The authors experimentally observe interference of ultracold fermionic atoms released from optical lattices and analyze the resulting patterns.
result: They extract signatures of short-range correlations and phase coherence in the fermionic Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that interference of fermionic gases can reveal correlation properties, extending techniques previously applied to bosons.

title: Chirality Cannot Be Ferroic In Phase Transitions Leading To Enantiomorphic Space-Group Pairs
authors: F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. Mccabe, A. H. Romero, And E. Bousquet
abstract:
Author(s): F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. McCabe, A. H. Romero, and E. Bousquet

With growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. In the work described, we demonstrate, by means of a formal group-theoretical proof and a systematic group-subgroup analysis, that achiral-to-chiral …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that chirality cannot be a ferroic order parameter in structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space-group pairs.
motivation: There is growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, and it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. The authors aim to clarify whether chirality can be ferroic.
method: The authors use formal group-theoretical proof and systematic group-subgroup analysis to examine achiral-to-chiral phase transitions.
result: They demonstrate that chirality cannot be ferroic in such transitions, as it does not satisfy the necessary symmetry conditions for a ferroic order parameter.
conclusion: Chirality should not be considered a ferroic property, which has implications for the classification of ferroic materials and the understanding of chiral phases.

title: Spin-Triplet Paired Wigner Crystal Stabilized By Quantum Geometry
authors: Dmitry Zverevich, Alex Levchenko, And Ilya Esterlis
abstract:

We have used variational states to analyze the effects of band geometry on the two-dimensional Wigner crystal with one and two electrons per unit cell. At sufficiently low electron densities, we find that increasing Berry curvature drives a transition into a crystalline state composed of spin-triple…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036506] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a spin-triplet paired Wigner crystal stabilized by quantum geometry, focusing on band geometry effects in a condensed matter system.
motivation: To understand how Berry curvature and band geometry influence the formation of crystalline states in low-density electron systems.
method: Variational wavefunction analysis of the two-dimensional Wigner crystal with one and two electrons per unit cell, incorporating band geometry.
result: Increasing Berry curvature drives a transition into a crystalline state composed of spin-triplet pairs.
conclusion: Quantum geometry can stabilize novel paired crystalline phases in electron systems.

title: Harnessing Spin-Texture Dynamics For Low-Noise, High-Sensitivity Magnetic Sensors
authors: Kang Wang, Teng Xu, Meng Shi, Xinxiang Sun, Yizhou Liu, Huali Yang, Run-Wei Li, And Haifeng Du

The development of low-noise, high-sensitivity magnetic sensors is essential for applications such as automotive systems, biomedical imaging, and magnetic microscopy. However, sensor performance has long been impeded by a fundamental constraint that noise and sensitivity increase concomitantly, whic…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036705] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to break the noise-sensitivity trade-off in magnetic sensors by exploiting spin-texture dynamics.
motivation: Magnetic sensors are limited by a fundamental trade-off between noise and sensitivity; the authors aim to overcome this constraint.
method: They utilize spin-texture dynamics, likely involving skyrmions or domain walls, to achieve simultaneous low noise and high sensitivity.
result: The proposed sensor demonstrates improved performance, breaking the conventional trade-off.
conclusion: Spin-texture dynamics offer a promising route for next-generation magnetic sensors.

title: Synchronization Driven Reciprocity Breaking
authors: Alexander K. Stoychev, Ulrich Kuhl, And Nicolas Noiray

Wave transmission reciprocity is broken by exploiting the synchronization of two coupled self-oscillators. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033802] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates non-reciprocal wave transmission by exploiting synchronization of coupled self-oscillators.
motivation: Breaking reciprocity in wave transmission is important for applications like isolators and circulators, but existing methods often require nonlinear materials or external magnetic fields.
method: The authors use two coupled self-oscillators that synchronize in phase or antiphase depending on the illumination port, leading to direction-dependent transmission.
result: They achieve reciprocity breaking through self-adjusting synchronization, without external bias.
conclusion: This approach offers a new mechanism for non-reciprocal devices based on synchronization dynamics.

title: Microwave Signature Of The Emerging Abrikosov Lattice Above ${H}_{c2}$
authors: Hang Zhou, Zhanghai Chen, A. A. Varlamov, Andreas Glatz, And Yuriy Yerin

tldr: This paper studies the microwave signature of the emerging Abrikosov lattice in type-II superconducting films above the upper critical field.
motivation: To understand the precursor effects of vortex lattice formation in the normal phase of superconductors, which is a fundamental aspect of condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and analysis of microwave conductivity fluctuations to predict a signature of the Abrikosov lattice above H_c2.
result: They find that the microwave response exhibits a characteristic feature indicating the onset of vortex lattice order even above the critical field.
conclusion: The work provides a way to detect the incipient vortex lattice via microwave spectroscopy, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Microscopic Evidence For A Zhang-Rice Triplet State In The Van Der Waals Antiferromagnet, ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$
authors: Beom Hyun Kim, Youjin Lee, Junik Hwang, Junghyun Kim, Je-Geun Park, And Seung-Ho Baek

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036505] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses NMR to verify a Zhang-Rice triplet ground state in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS3.
motivation: Understanding the magnetic ground state of NiPS3 is important for its potential in spintronics and other applications.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements were performed on NiPS3 single crystals to probe the local magnetic environment.
result: The NMR data confirm the existence of a Zhang-Rice triplet state, resolving previous ambiguities about the ground state.
conclusion: The Zhang-Rice triplet is the correct ground state for NiPS3, providing a foundation for further studies of its magnetic properties.

title: Photoinduced Switching Of Magnetization In The Epsilon-Near-Zero Regime
authors: Héloïse Damas, Carl S. Davies, Petr M. Vetoshko, Vladimir I. Belotelov, Andrzej Stupakiewicz, And Andrei Kirilyuk

Midinfrared laser pulses tuned to optical phonon frequencies can induce magnetization switching in magnetic dielectrics, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear, since excitations of the crystal lattice can simultaneously produce heating and nonthermal strain. Here, we study the response of lab…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036704] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced magnetization switching in magnetic dielectrics using midinfrared laser pulses tuned to optical phonon frequencies.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms of ultrafast magnetization switching is important for spintronics and data storage, but the role of lattice excitations versus thermal effects is unclear.
method: The authors experimentally investigate the response of a magnetic dielectric to midinfrared laser pulses in the epsilon-near-zero regime, analyzing magnetization dynamics.
result: They observe magnetization switching induced by the laser pulses and attribute it to nonthermal strain rather than heating.
conclusion: The work provides insight into photoinduced magnetization switching mechanisms, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics study with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Directional Photocurrent Generated By Quantum Interference Control
authors: Yiming Gong, Kai Wang, And Steven T. Cundiff
abstract:

motivation: To achieve directional control of photocurrent without external fields, enabling new optoelectronic applications.
method: Using quantum interference control with tailored optical pulses to generate a directional photocurrent beam.
result: Demonstrated an 'electron lighthouse' that produces highly directional 2D beams of photocurrent.
conclusion: Quantum interference control can be used to steer photocurrent directionally, with potential for novel optoelectronic devices.

authors: Isak Cecil Onsager Rukan, Jan Gulla, And Johannes Skaar
abstract:

motivation: To explore the quantum effects of time-dependent boundary conditions on photon states.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the scenario of a single photon reflecting off a mirror that is suddenly removed, using quantum field theory in a cavity.
result: The removal of the mirror transforms the single-photon state into a superposition of multi-photon states, demonstrating non-trivial quantum dynamics.
conclusion: Time-varying optical boundaries can generate complex quantum states, with potential implications for quantum optics and information.

title: Superradiant Parametric Mössbauer Radiation Source
authors: Ze-An Peng, Christoph H. Keitel, And Jörg Evers

motivation: Future applications of Mössbauer nuclei require x-ray sources with exceptionally high peak and average spectral flux, which are not available with current sources.
method: The authors introduce a scheme based on scattering of spatially microstructured electron beams from Mössbauer nuclei to achieve superradiant parametric emission.
result: The proposed source can produce intense, narrow-band x-ray radiation with enhanced flux compared to conventional Mössbauer sources.
conclusion: The SPMR source could enable new applications in nuclear quantum optics and precision spectroscopy.

title: Kondo Effect In Nonreciprocal Response
authors: Hajime Murata And Hiroaki Ishizuka

Chiral magnetic states give rise to rich phenomena, from the anomalous Hall effect and the nonlinear electrical current to multiferroics and magnetochiral dichroism. method: The authors theoretically analyze the Kondo effect in a model of chiral magnets, calculating the nonreciprocal electrical response using perturbation theory and numerical methods.
result: They find that the Kondo effect can significantly enhance nonreciprocal transport, leading to a large magnetochiral anisotropy.
conclusion: The Kondo effect is an important mechanism for nonreciprocal response in chiral magnets, with potential implications for spintronics and quantum materials.

title: Nonlinear Odd Viscoelastic Effect
authors: Ashwat Jain, Wojciech J. Jankowski, M. Mehraeen, And Robert-Jan Slager

motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum geometry and viscoelastic response in topological materials.
method: The authors derive nonlinear viscoelastic response functions from higher-order quantum geometric tensors in magnetic three-dimensional topological phases.
result: They identify odd viscoelastic effects that are nonlinear and tied to the topological nature of the material.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of odd viscosity to nonlinear regimes and connects it to quantum geometry, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct application to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Even Denominator Fractional Quantum Hall States In The Zeroth Landau Level Of Aba Trilayer Graphene
authors: Tanima Chanda, Simrandeep Kaur, Harsimran Singh, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Manish Jain, Udit Khanna, Ajit C. Balram, And Aveek Bid

motivation: Even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states are of particular interest because they can host non-Abelian quasiparticles, which are important for topological quantum computing. The zeroth Landau level in trilayer graphene was previously thought to be unpolarized, making such states unexpected.
method: The authors performed transport measurements on ABA trilayer graphene devices at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, identifying fractional quantum Hall states at half-filling in the zeroth Landau level.
result: They observed even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states at filling factors 1/2 and 3/2 in the zeroth Landau level, challenging the conventional expectation that such states are absent in this regime.
conclusion: The discovery of these states in trilayer graphene opens new avenues for studying non-Abelian quasiparticles and topological quantum computation in a new material platform.

title: Demonstration Of Deuterium’s Enhanced Sensitivity To Symmetry Violations Governed By The Standard-Model Extension

motivation: To test fundamental symmetries (Lorentz and CPT) by looking for sidereal variations in hyperfine transition frequencies of deuterium.
method: Hyperfine spectroscopy of two transitions in ground-state deuterium, analyzing data for sidereal variations to constrain nonrelativistic proton coefficients in the Standard-Model Extension.
result: No evidence of Lorentz or CPT violation was found, setting improved constraints on certain SME coefficients.
conclusion: The results provide the most stringent limits on some proton-sector SME coefficients, but do not directly advance the user's core research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

tldr: This paper studies the ground state phase diagram of a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with competing interactions, revealing a nematic Luttinger liquid phase.
motivation: To understand the zero-magnetization Mott transition and emergent phases in strongly correlated spin chains without external magnetic field.
method: Uses density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations to compute the phase diagram.
result: Identifies a commensurate-incommensurate Mott transition and the emergence of a nematic Luttinger liquid phase.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into quantum phases in frustrated spin chains, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pseudochiral Phonons From Octupolar Magnetic Order

tldr: This paper introduces pseudochiral phonons in multipolar magnets, focusing on a condensed matter phenomenon without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Recent discovery of large magnetic response of chiral phonons in dipolar magnets motivates exploring similar effects in multipolar magnets.
method: The authors theoretically analyze Raman active quantum phonons in multipolar magnets, introducing the concept of pseudochiral phonons.
result: They show that pseudochiral phonons emerge in multipolar magnets, analogous to chiral phonons in dipolar magnets.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of phonon-magnetic interactions to multipolar systems, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Interelectronic Correlation: Neutral And Ionized Atoms In Conjugate Spaces
authors: M. M. Gutiérrez-Vílchez, I. López-García, And J. C. Angulo

tldr: This paper quantifies interelectronic correlation in multielectronic systems using electron-pair densities and mutual information.
motivation: Understanding electron correlation is fundamental to atomic and molecular physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors compare the electron-pair density with the product of one-particle densities to define a correlation measure, and analyze it in conjugate spaces.
result: They derive expressions for the correlation measure and apply it to neutral and ionized atoms.
conclusion: The work provides a new way to quantify electron correlation but remains within atomic physics without implications for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of Nonlinear Spin Dynamics In Dual-cell Atomic Gases

tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of nonlinear spin dynamics in dual-cell atomic gases, focusing on spin masers and time crystals.

method: The authors use a dual-cell atomic gas setup to observe nonlinear spin dynamics, likely involving optical pumping and spin-exchange collisions.
result: They observe nonlinear dynamical phases predicted by recent theory, demonstrating controlled spin dynamics in a dual-cell configuration.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for nonlinear spin dynamics, advancing the understanding of spin masers and time crystals.

title: Non-Abelian Topological Charges Determined By Euler Class
authors: Yu Huang, Jiayun Ning, Keran Hu, Linsheng Bao, Aoqian Shi, Shilong Li, And Jianjun Liu

title: Enantiosensitive Exceptional Points In Open Chiral Systems
authors: Nicola Mayer, Alexander Löhr, Nimrod Moiseyev, Misha Ivanov, And Olga Smirnova

title: Optical Probes Of Coherence In Two-dimensional Bose Gases Of Polaritons
authors: Joseph Jachinowski, Hassan Alnatah, David W. Snoke, And Peter B. Littlewood
abstract:

authors: S. K. Mahatha, A. Kar, J. Corral-Sertal, Josu Diego, A. Korshunov, C.-Y. Lim, F. K. Diekmann, D. Subires, J. Phillips, T. K. Kim, D. Ishikawa, G. Marini, I. Vobornik, Ion Errea, S. Rohlf, M. However, the underlying, material-specific, microscopic mechanisms often remain unclear. Here, we unveil a high-temperature incommensurate charge-order…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065120] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a first-order phase transition driven by competing charge-order fluctuations in 1T'-TaTe2, focusing on the microscopic mechanism of the transition.
motivation: First-order phase transitions are common but their microscopic origins are often unclear; this work aims to uncover the mechanism in a specific material.
method: The authors use experimental techniques (likely X-ray scattering, spectroscopy) and theoretical modeling to study charge-order fluctuations and their competition.
result: They identify that competing charge-order fluctuations drive the first-order phase transition in 1T'-TaTe2.
conclusion: The study provides insight into the microscopic mechanism of first-order phase transitions in this material, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emergent Anomalous Hall Effect From Surface States In Altermagnetic MnTe Thin Films
authors: Yufei Zhao, Saswata Mandal, Chao-Xing Liu, And Binghai Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Yufei Zhao, Saswata Mandal, Chao-Xing Liu, and Binghai Yan

Transport measurements on thin films of the prototypical altermagnet MnTe have yielded conflicting reports including the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) with opposite signs and resistivity independent of thickness. In this work, we resolve these discrepancies by disentangling the bulk and surface contri…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065304] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves conflicting transport measurements in altermagnetic MnTe thin films by disentangling bulk and surface contributions to the anomalous Hall effect.
motivation: Experimental reports on the anomalous Hall effect in MnTe thin films show conflicting signs and thickness-independent resistivity, which need to be resolved.
method: The authors theoretically model the electronic structure and transport properties of MnTe thin films, separating surface state contributions from bulk altermagnetic effects.
result: They find that surface states can dominate the anomalous Hall effect, explaining the sign changes and thickness independence observed in experiments.
conclusion: The anomalous Hall effect in MnTe thin films arises from surface states rather than intrinsic altermagnetic order, reconciling previous discrepancies.

title: Kinetic Magnetism And Stripe Order In The Antiferromagnetic Bosonic $t\text{−}J$ Model
authors: Timothy J. Harris, Ulrich Schollwöck, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Timothy J. Harris, Ulrich Schollwöck, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

How can particle statistics influence the competition between charge motion and magnetic order in doped antiferromagnets? Here, the authors use large-scale numerical calculations to establish the =0 phase diagram of the 2D antiferromagnetic bosonic
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051105] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of the antiferromagnetic bosonic t-J model, focusing on kinetic magnetism and stripe order.
motivation: To understand how particle statistics affect the competition between charge motion and magnetic order in doped antiferromagnets.
method: Large-scale numerical calculations (likely DMRG or tensor networks) to map out the zero-temperature phase diagram of the 2D bosonic t-J model.
result: Mobile bosonic holes stabilize partially filled stripes at low doping and drive transitions to polarized ferromagnetic phases via Nagaoka polaron formation.
conclusion: The predictions provide clear targets for future experiments in ultracold-atom quantum simulators.

title: Charged Moiré Phonons In Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Alejandro Ramos-Alonso And Héctor Ochoa
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Ramos-Alonso and Héctor Ochoa

Moiré phonons describe collective vibrations of a moiré superlattice produced by long-wavelength relative displacements of the constituent layers. Despite coming from the backfolding of the acoustic phonons of the individual layers, many of these modes become infrared active when the system is doped…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051106] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies moiré phonons in twisted bilayer graphene, focusing on their infrared activity upon doping.
motivation: Understanding the vibrational properties of moiré superlattices in twisted bilayer graphene is important for characterizing its electronic and optical properties.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the collective vibrations (moiré phonons) arising from long-wavelength relative displacements of the layers and compute their infrared activity when the system is doped.
result: Many moiré phonon modes become infrared active upon doping, which can be probed experimentally.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the lattice dynamics of twisted bilayer graphene, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Effects Of Decoherence On Fermi's Golden Rule
authors: Caihong Zheng And Fan Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Caihong Zheng and Fan Zheng

Fermi's golden rule, which describes the transition rates between two electronic levels under external stimulations, is used ubiquitously in different fields of physics. The original Fermi's golden rule was derived from perturbative time-dependent Schrödinger's equation without the direct contributi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014309] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies decoherence effects on Fermi's golden rule in a condensed matter context.
motivation: Fermi's golden rule is widely used but its validity under decoherence is not well understood.
method: The authors derive modified transition rates by incorporating decoherence into the perturbative treatment.
result: Decoherence modifies the transition rates and can suppress or enhance them depending on parameters.
conclusion: The standard Fermi's golden rule may need corrections in the presence of strong decoherence.

title: Pressure-induced Structural Transitions And Dome-shaped Superconductivity In The Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{PbBi}}_{6}{\mathrm{Te}}_{10}$
authors: Junying Hu, Guangyang Dai, Liang Ma, Jingkai Bi, Jianyong Chen, And Zhiwei Men
abstract:
