Topological insulators (TIs) constitute a unique class of quantum materials owing to their topology-protected electron states. While pressure is an effective way to induce superconductivity in TIs, superconductivity often appears after phase transition or structural disorder. Therefore, identifying …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024103] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pressure-induced structural transitions and superconductivity in the topological insulator PbBi6Te10.
motivation: Topological insulators can host superconductivity under pressure, but the relationship between structural changes and superconductivity is not well understood.
method: The authors perform high-pressure experiments, including X-ray diffraction and electrical transport measurements, to track structural and superconducting properties.
result: They observe a dome-shaped superconducting phase and identify structural transitions that correlate with the emergence of superconductivity.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the interplay between structural disorder and superconductivity in topological insulators.

title: Design Of Nearly Flat Band Models With Arbitrary Chern Numbers
authors: Jing-Min Fan, Fan-Di Sun, Ai-Lei He, Wei-Wei Luo, And Yi-Fei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-Min Fan, Fan-Di Sun, Ai-Lei He, Wei-Wei Luo, and Yi-Fei Wang

This work develops a method for constructing nearly flat bands with arbitrary Chern number [MATH] in momentum space and further reconstructing their corresponding real-space models. In the two-band case, starting from a known topological flat band with [MATH], we systematically generate nearly flat band…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055116] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to construct nearly flat band models with arbitrary Chern numbers in momentum space and reconstruct their real-space models.
motivation: Flat bands with nontrivial topology are of interest for strongly correlated physics, but existing models are limited to specific Chern numbers. The authors aim to provide a systematic construction for arbitrary Chern numbers.
method: Starting from a known topological flat band with Chern number C=1, the authors use a combination of momentum-space transformations and real-space reconstruction to generate models with higher Chern numbers.
result: They demonstrate the construction for several Chern numbers and show that the resulting bands remain nearly flat with nontrivial topology.
conclusion: The method provides a flexible framework for designing flat band models with desired Chern numbers, which may be useful for studying fractional Chern insulators and other topological phases.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely attributed to spontaneous O(2) symmetry breaking, but the authors suspect this is incorrect.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model and analyze its symmetry properties using analytical arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They show that the model lacks O(2) symmetry and that the observed transition is not due to symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The conventional understanding of the Vicsek model's phase transition is flawed, and a new explanation is needed.

title: First-passage Times For The Space-fractional Fokker-Planck Equation
authors: Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, And Boris Z. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, and Boris Z. Huang

We extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps, providing first-passage time (FPT) properties for a class of superdiffusive processes which are governed by the space-fractional spectral Fokker-Planck equation. This first-passage process introduces FPT properties, different from Lévy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014136] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of step correlations.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into first-passage phenomena in superdiffusive processes, but it is not relevant to the specified research directions.

title: Optimal Navigation In Two-dimensional Flows: Control Theory And Reinforcement Learning
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir Parfenyev

Zermelo's navigation problem seeks the trajectory of minimal travel time between two points in a fluid flow. We address this problem for an agent—such as a floating drone or active particle—that is advected by a two-dimensional flow, self-propels at a fixed speed smaller than or comparable to the ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015104] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves Zermelo's navigation problem for an agent in a two-dimensional flow using control theory and reinforcement learning.
motivation: Finding optimal paths in fluid flows is important for autonomous vehicles and active particles, but classical methods may be computationally expensive.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a time-optimal control problem and apply reinforcement learning to approximate the optimal policy.
result: They demonstrate that reinforcement learning can efficiently find near-optimal trajectories in various flow fields.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning offers a practical approach to navigation in complex flows, though the work is primarily applied and lacks quantum or thermodynamic depth.

title: Localization-delocalization Transition In Low-dimensional Asymmetric Resetting Random Walks
authors: Reza Sepehrinia

Author(s): Reza Sepehrinia

We investigate biased random walks with stochastic resetting to previously visited sites and demonstrate how directional drift fundamentally alters the emergence of localized stationary states. We show that bias acts as a competing mechanism and can weaken or suppress localization. This competition …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014128] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of directional drift on localization in resetting random walks.
motivation: To understand how bias alters the stationary state of random walks with stochastic resetting.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of biased random walks with resetting to previously visited sites.
result: Bias weakens or suppresses localization, leading to a localization-delocalization transition.
conclusion: Directional drift competes with resetting, fundamentally changing the emergence of localized states.

title: Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time And Jump-length Distributions As A Model Of Biased Anomalous Transport
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, and Ralf Metzler

Continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are highly appreciated as a model of anomalous diffusion (AD) in complex media such as structured and heterogeneous environments. These walks are used to describe AD phenomena characterized by a nonlinear functional dependence of the mean-squared displacement (MS…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion is common in complex media, and biased transport (e.g., under external fields) is important for many physical systems. The authors aim to generalize CTRW models to include asymmetry in both waiting times and jump lengths.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the mean-squared displacement and other transport characteristics for CTRWs with coupled asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions, using generating functions and Laplace-Fourier transforms.
result: They find that asymmetry in waiting times and jump lengths can lead to a variety of anomalous diffusion regimes, including subdiffusion, superdiffusion, and ballistic motion, depending on the parameters.
conclusion: The model provides a flexible framework for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous media, with potential applications in biology and materials science.

title: Universality Of Order Statistics For Brownian Reshuffling
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, And Tomasz Maciocha
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, and Tomasz Maciocha

In a one-dimensional gas of particles confined by an asymptotically power-law potential, the ordering of the particles changes as they perform Brownian motion. The authors show that the order statistics that describe how the particles are reshuffled are universal and independent of the potential’s exponent, while the timescale of the reshuffling does depend on it.

#UniversalBehavior #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014130] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the universality of order statistics in a one-dimensional gas of Brownian particles confined by a power-law potential.
motivation: Understanding how particle ordering changes over time in a diffusive system is a fundamental statistical mechanics problem with potential applications in soft matter and biological physics.
method: The authors analytically derive the order statistics for Brownian particles in a power-law potential, showing that the reshuffling dynamics are universal and independent of the potential exponent, while the timescale depends on it.
result: The order statistics describing particle reshuffling are universal, but the timescale of reshuffling depends on the potential exponent.
conclusion: The work provides a universal characterization of order statistics in a class of diffusive systems, highlighting the interplay between confinement and diffusion.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network

motivation: Understanding how electric fields affect neuronal network dynamics is important for neuroscience, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of a FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal network with hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields in a ring topology.
result: Observed collective behaviors including incoherent activity, coherent traveling waves, and chimera states.
conclusion: The study provides insights into neuronal network dynamics but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles

Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate of Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity between stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research.
method: The authors define a distance metric using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove its properties.
result: The proposed distance function is a valid metric and can be computed efficiently for finite-state Markov chains.
conclusion: The distance function provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes modeled as Markov chains.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential to derive the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically and numerically to compute the intermediate scattering function for an overdamped Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential.
result: They derive a general expression for the ISF and analyze its dependence on tilt and potential strength.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed classical statistical mechanics result but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Floquet Resonances In The Double Kicked Top

We study exact quantum resonances in the double kicked top (DKT), a driven spin model that extends the quantum kicked top (QKT) by introducing an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick. By expressing the dynamics in terms of effective parameters [MATH], we analytically show the…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014214] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.

motivation: To understand quantum resonance phenomena in a periodically driven system with broken time-reversal symmetry.
method: Analytical derivation of effective parameters and analysis of the Floquet operator.
result: Exact conditions for quantum resonances are identified and characterized.
conclusion: The double kicked top exhibits rich resonance behavior that can be analytically understood.

title: Emergence Of Higher-order Interactions In Systems Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators With Time Delay

We show that higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators. By expanding the delayed pairwise coupling to the second order, we derive a delay-free Kuramoto model possessing both pairwise and three-body interactions. Numerical simulations and s…

motivation: To understand how higher-order interactions can arise from simple pairwise couplings with time delay in oscillator networks.
method: The delayed pairwise coupling is expanded to second order, deriving a delay-free Kuramoto model with pairwise and three-body interactions; numerical simulations and stability analysis are performed.
result: Higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling, and the derived model captures the dynamics.
conclusion: Time delay in pairwise coupling can effectively generate higher-order interactions, which may be relevant for complex systems.

tldr: This paper studies random walks on disordered lattices to model solute transport in porous media, focusing on effective diffusion coefficients.
motivation: Understanding diffusion in porous materials is important for applications like contaminant transport, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of random walks on 3D lattices with random and periodic blocked sites, analyzing effective diffusion coefficients as a function of porosity.
result: The effective diffusion coefficient depends on porosity and spatial correlations, with applications to diffusive transport in porous materials.
conclusion: The study provides insights into classical diffusion in disordered media but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Different Phases And Phase Transition Points In Hidden Markov Models

method: Analyzes stationary solutions of the master equation for hidden Markov models.
result: Discovers different phases with localized or delocalized stationary distributions and hypothesizes phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of phases in HMMs but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper studies alternating pattern formation in oscillatory media with global feedback, applied to chemical and biological systems.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms behind alternating stripes, clusters, and labyrinths observed in chemical reactions and biological systems like Min-protein dynamics and cardiac alternans.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of oscillatory media with spatially uniform and nonuniform global feedback.
result: Identified conditions and mechanisms leading to alternating pattern formation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into spatiotemporal pattern formation in oscillatory media, relevant to biological and chemical contexts.

title: Unified Ott-Antonsen Framework For Stability And Bifurcations In Ring Swarmalators
authors: Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, And Xingang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, and Xingang Wang

Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014212] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for analyzing stability and bifurcations in ring swarmalator systems, which combine phase oscillations with spatial swarming.
motivation: Swarmalators exhibit rich collective dynamics, but a general theoretical framework for their stability and bifurcations was lacking.
method: The authors extend the Ott-Antonsen ansatz to ring swarmalator models, deriving reduced equations for the macroscopic order parameters.
result: They obtain analytical conditions for synchronization, clustering, and traveling waves, and characterize bifurcation scenarios.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a powerful tool for understanding collective behavior in active matter systems with both phase and spatial degrees of freedom.

title: Statistical Mechanics Of Indistinguishable Energy States And The Glass Transition
authors: Shimul Akhanjee
abstract:
Author(s): Shimul Akhanjee

The statistical mechanics of particles that populate indistinguishable energy substates is explored. In particular, the mathematical treatment of microstates differs from conventional statistical mechanics, where, for a given degeneracy, the energy sublevels or substates are universally treated as d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014119] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a modified statistical mechanics for indistinguishable energy substates to model the glass transition.
motivation: Standard statistical mechanics treats degenerate energy levels as distinguishable, which may not capture the physics of glassy systems where substates are indistinguishable.
method: The author develops a mathematical framework where microstates are counted differently for indistinguishable energy substates, altering the partition function and thermodynamic quantities.
result: The new formalism predicts a glass transition temperature and reproduces key features of glassy dynamics, such as a Kauzmann-like entropy crisis.
conclusion: Indistinguishability of energy substates may be a fundamental principle underlying the glass transition, offering a new perspective on the statistical mechanics of disordered systems.

title: Twisted State Stability Under Local Order Parameter Adaptation
authors: Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, And Ya Jia

tldr: This paper studies the stability of twisted states in nonlocally coupled ring networks with higher-order interactions and adaptive coupling based on local order parameters.
motivation: Twisted states are common in coupled oscillator networks, and understanding their stability under adaptive mechanisms is important for controlling synchronization patterns.
method: The authors analyze a ring network of phase oscillators with higher-order (simplicial) interactions and introduce an adaptive feedback that adjusts coupling strengths based on the local order parameter. They perform linear stability analysis and numerical simulations.
result: They derive stability conditions for twisted states and show that the adaptive mechanism can stabilize or destabilize certain twisted states depending on parameters.
conclusion: The adaptive local order parameter feedback provides a way to control twisted state stability in networks with higher-order interactions.

title: Quantum Nanorotator In The Hypomagnetic Field: Implications For Magnetobiology
authors: V. N. Binhi

method: Models a molecular rotator in an enzyme cavity with quantum decoherence and rotational dynamics.
result: Shows that a nanoscale rotator can have long decoherence times and respond to hypomagnetic fields.
conclusion: The quantum nanorotator model provides a plausible mechanism for magnetobiology effects.

title: Autoparametric Excitation Of An Elastic Chain In A Periodic Potential
authors: Johann Maddi, Christophe Coste, And Michel Saint Jean
abstract:

We describe the motions of an elastic chain submitted to an external periodic potential, without dissipation. Initially, the energy is injected in a single eigenmode of the chain. [Phys. Rev. E 114, 015504] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the autoparametric excitation of an elastic chain in a periodic potential without dissipation, focusing on energy transfer between eigenmodes.
motivation: To understand how energy injected into a single eigenmode of an elastic chain can parametrically excite other modes in the absence of external energy sources.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of an elastic chain under a periodic potential, modeling the energy injection into one eigenmode and deriving conditions for parametric excitation of other modes.
result: They show that the initially excited eigenmode acts as a parametric forcing for other modes, leading to energy transfer and complex dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear mode coupling in elastic systems, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Structure And Memory Control Self-diffusion In Active Matter
authors: Akinlade Akintunde And Stewart A. Mallory
abstract:
Author(s): Akinlade Akintunde and Stewart A. Mallory

Despite extensive progress in characterizing the emergent behavior of active matter, the microscopic origins of self-diffusion in interacting active systems remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a framework that quantitatively links self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014115] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a framework linking self-diffusion in active matter to collisional forces and their temporal correlations.
motivation: The microscopic origins of self-diffusion in interacting active systems are poorly understood despite progress in characterizing emergent behavior.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that quantitatively connects self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correlations.
result: The framework provides a quantitative link between structure, memory, and self-diffusion in active matter.
conclusion: The study advances understanding of self-diffusion in active matter by revealing the role of collisional forces and memory effects.

title: Quantum-classical Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo With Matchgate Shadows On Trapped Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Luning Zhao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Luning Zhao et al.

We demonstrate an end-to-end workflow to model chemical reaction barriers with the quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) algorithm with quantum tomography using matchgate shadows. The workflow operates within an accelerated quantum supercomputing environment with the IonQ …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033061] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum-classical hybrid algorithm for quantum chemistry using matchgate shadows on trapped ion quantum computers.
motivation: To model chemical reaction barriers accurately using near-term quantum devices by combining quantum Monte Carlo with quantum tomography.
method: The workflow uses auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) with matchgate shadows for efficient tomography on trapped ion quantum computers.
result: The algorithm successfully computes reaction barrier heights with improved accuracy compared to classical methods, demonstrating feasibility on current hardware.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach shows promise for practical quantum chemistry simulations on near-term quantum computers.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals
authors: L. A. Rüffert And T. E. Mehlstäubler
abstract:
Author(s): L. A. Rüffert and T. E. Mehlstäubler

Self-organized three-dimensional (3D) ion Coulomb crystals in linear Paul traps naturally form concentric shells that provide a curved, atomically resolved interface for studying two-dimensional (2D) nanofriction. Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical many-body physics and nanofriction, not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding nanofriction at the atomic scale is important for fundamental physics and applications, and ion crystals provide a clean platform to study these effects.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations of 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap to investigate the formation of concentric shells and the frictional forces between them.
result: They observe that the shells form a curved interface and exhibit two-dimensional nanofriction with stick-slip dynamics, and characterize the dependence on system parameters.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that 3D ion crystals are a versatile platform for studying nanofriction, but the results are primarily classical and do not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, And Justin C. W. Song
abstract:
Author(s): Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, and Justin C. W. Song

The quantum states in doubly degenerate Kramers pairs can act as an internal degree of freedom. Here, we uncover a Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets: interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light irradiation can selectively polarize Kramers partnered states allowing to control …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033046] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets, a condensed matter phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnets, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect where interband transitions selectively polarize Kramers partnered states.
conclusion: This effect provides a mechanism to control Kramers pairs, which may have applications in spintronics or optoelectronics, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Virgile Troude and Didier Sornette

Heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics pervade physics, finance, and economics, yet their origin is often ascribed to systems poised near criticality. Here, we show that such behavior can emerge far from instability through a universal mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033050] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a mechanism for heavy-tailed fluctuations via non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: Heavy-tailed fluctuations are common in physics, finance, and economics, often attributed to criticality. The authors aim to show they can arise from a different, universal mechanism.
method: The authors analyze multidimensional Kesten processes and demonstrate that non-normal eigenvector amplification can generate heavy-tailed statistics without instability.
result: They show that non-normal amplification leads to power-law distributions, providing a new mechanism for heavy tails.
conclusion: Heavy-tailed fluctuations can emerge far from criticality through non-normal eigenvector amplification, offering a broader explanation for such phenomena.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice
authors: Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú And Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú and Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz

Artificial colloidal ice is an icelike system used to study the effects of frustration in controlled environments, where all degrees of freedom can be accessed at a length scale large enough for optical visualization and in real time. We modify this model system by inducing anisotropic interactions …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033051] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical spin freezing in artificial colloidal ice with anisotropic interactions, a condensed matter system not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how anisotropic interactions affect the dynamics of frustrated artificial spin ice systems, which are classical analogs of magnetic materials.
method: Experimental realization of artificial colloidal ice with tunable anisotropic interactions via optical traps, combined with real-time imaging and analysis of spin dynamics.
result: Anisotropic interactions induce a dynamical freezing transition where spins become trapped in metastable configurations, slowing down relaxation.
conclusion: Anisotropic interactions can be used to control the dynamics of artificial spin ice, offering insights into frustration and glassy behavior in classical systems.

title: Ultracold Amplification Proposal For Parity Violation In Chiral Molecules
authors: Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, And Salvador Miret-Artés
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, and Salvador Miret-Artés

We propose a theoretical mechanism to indirectly detect the small parity-violating energy difference (PVED) between chiral enantiomers through a macroscopic enantiomeric excess observed in an ultracold gas. We consider that chiral molecules are formed resonantly via ultracold collisions of achiral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033056] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a theoretical mechanism to detect parity violation in chiral molecules via ultracold gas amplification.
motivation: Parity-violating energy differences (PVED) in chiral molecules are extremely small and have not been directly observed; the authors aim to amplify the effect to detectable levels.
method: They model ultracold collisions of achiral fragments that resonantly form chiral molecules, and analyze how a small PVED can lead to a macroscopic enantiomeric excess through a kinetic amplification mechanism.
result: The mechanism predicts that under ultracold conditions, the tiny PVED can be amplified into a measurable enantiomeric excess, enabling indirect detection.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a viable path to observe parity violation in chiral molecules, which has implications for fundamental physics and chemistry.

title: Topological States And Flat Bands In Exactly Solvable Decorated Cayley Trees
authors: Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, And Tomáš Bzdušek
abstract:
Author(s): Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, and Tomáš Bzdušek

We derive the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that constitute tree analogs of selected two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, namely, the Lieb, the double-Lieb, the kagome, and the star lattice. The common feature of these Euclidean lattices is that their nearest-neighbor models give rise to fl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033036] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that are tree analogs of certain two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, revealing flat bands and topological states.
motivation: To understand the spectral and topological properties of tree-like structures that mimic flat-band lattices, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors construct decorated Cayley trees corresponding to the Lieb, double-Lieb, kagome, and star lattices and solve the tight-binding model exactly using recursive techniques.
result: They obtain the complete energy spectrum and identify flat bands and topological edge states in these tree structures.
conclusion: Decorated Cayley trees provide exactly solvable models that capture key features of their Euclidean counterparts, offering insights into flat-band physics and topology.

title: Emergence Of Bistability And Even-order Harmonic Generation In A Centrosymmetric System Under Periodic Driving
authors: Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, And Ryo Shimano
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, and Ryo Shimano

Nonequilibrium states of matter, when driven periodically, can exhibit exotic properties and emergent behaviors that are fundamentally distinct from those in equilibrium systems. To investigate the dynamical behavior of a particle system under time-periodic external forces, we performed numerical si…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033041] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system under periodic driving, using numerical simulations.
motivation: To explore emergent nonequilibrium behaviors in periodically driven systems that are distinct from equilibrium.
method: Numerical simulations of a particle system under time-periodic external forces.
result: Observation of bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system.
conclusion: Periodic driving can induce exotic properties like bistability and even-order harmonics in centrosymmetric systems.

title: Quantum Physics-informed Neural Network With Residual-based Adaptive Refinement For Solving Partial Differential Equations
authors: Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, And Zhichao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, and Zhichao Zhang

In this paper, we propose a quantum physics-informed neural network (QPINN) to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by using residual-based adaptive refinement (RAR). The method incorporates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism into the training of QPINN, which aims to enhance conver…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033042] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum physics-informed neural network with residual-based adaptive refinement for solving partial differential equations.
motivation: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are promising for solving PDEs but suffer from convergence issues; quantum neural networks may offer advantages.
method: The authors design a quantum neural network architecture that incorporates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism to focus training on regions with high error.
result: The QPINN with RAR achieves improved accuracy and convergence compared to standard PINNs on benchmark PDEs.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks can enhance PINN performance for solving PDEs, but the work is primarily a numerical method without deep quantum information or thermodynamics insights.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in vdW heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time-resolved spectroscopy and theoretical modeling to probe charge transfer dynamics at different excitation energies.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways that depend on excitation energy, revealing how energy tuning can steer charge transfer.
conclusion: Controlling excitation energy provides a means to optimize charge separation in vdW heterostructures for optoelectronic applications.

title: Particle-hole Origin Of Thermal Beating In Dipole-compression Modes Of A One-dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, And Giulia de Rosi
abstract:
Author(s): Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, and Giulia De Rosi

This work reports a beating signal of two dipole-compression collective mode frequencies evolving from the low-temperature phononic hydrodynamic regime to the collisionless limit at the hole-induced anomaly temperature. The lower (higher) frequency originates from hole (particle) spectral states, and the temperature dependence of their relative excitation strengths reflects the thermal population imbalance between particle and hole states across the anomaly temperature.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032003] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal beating in dipole-compression modes of a 1D Bose gas, attributing it to particle-hole spectral states.
motivation: Understanding collective mode behavior in ultracold gases across temperature regimes is important for many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze the temperature dependence of two dipole-compression mode frequencies using a particle-hole picture and compare with experimental data.
result: They find that the lower frequency originates from hole states and the higher from particle states, with relative excitation strengths reflecting thermal population imbalance.
conclusion: The beating signal arises from the interplay of particle and hole excitations, providing insight into the crossover from hydrodynamic to collisionless regimes.

title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampling To Model Lagrangian Tracer Dispersion In Turbulent Boundary Layer
authors: Fabian Schindler And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Schindler and Jörg Schumacher

We present a quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QE-MCMC) method to sample turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution that depends on all three components and height to model the transport and dispersion of massless Lagrangian tracer particles in two different turbulent s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033031] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo to model Lagrangian tracer dispersion in turbulent boundary layers, a computational fluid dynamics problem.
motivation: Accurate modeling of turbulent particle dispersion is important for environmental and engineering applications, but classical MCMC can be computationally expensive.
method: The authors propose a quantum-enhanced MCMC algorithm that uses a quantum computer to accelerate sampling from the joint target distribution of turbulent acceleration vectors.
result: The QE-MCMC method demonstrates improved sampling efficiency compared to classical MCMC for the specific turbulent flow scenarios considered.
conclusion: Quantum computing can offer advantages for certain sampling tasks in fluid dynamics, but the practical impact depends on future hardware development.

title: Noiseless Limit And Improved-prior Limit Of The Maximum Entropy Method And Their Implications For The Analytic Continuation Problem
authors: Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, And Tobias Dornheim
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, and Tobias Dornheim

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are uniquely capable of providing exact simulations of quantum many-body systems. Unfortunately, the applications of a QMC simulation are limited because extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem. Across the many fields that us…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033009] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the maximum entropy method for analytic continuation in quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on its noiseless and improved-prior limits.
motivation: Quantum Monte Carlo methods provide exact simulations of quantum many-body systems, but extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem, which is ill-posed.
method: The authors study the maximum entropy method in the noiseless limit and with improved priors, deriving theoretical bounds and testing on synthetic data.
result: They show that in the noiseless limit, the method can recover exact spectral functions, and improved priors reduce bias and variance.
conclusion: The findings provide guidance for choosing priors and noise levels in practical analytic continuation, improving reliability of dynamic property extraction from QMC data.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, and Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a novel phase of matter that could host exotic quasiparticles, but experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy was used to measure the out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response of the MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: The observed antiferromagnetic response provides experimental signatures consistent with a putative fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings suggest that twisted MoTe2 is a promising platform for realizing fractional topological insulators, but further confirmation is needed.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields on a classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum mechanics with classical gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum field theory and general relativity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, providing a testable framework for the nature of spacetime.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral formalism that couples quantum fields to a classical stochastic spacetime, incorporating backreaction through a consistent semiclassical approach.
result: They derive a consistent mathematical framework that yields well-defined dynamics for both quantum fields and classical spacetime, with potential observational consequences.
conclusion: The framework offers a viable semiclassical approach to quantum gravity that can be tested experimentally, suggesting that spacetime may not require a full quantum description.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for designing nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and classical molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer binding and sliding resistance in h-BN.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate interlayer binding and friction, offering a potential mechanism for active control.
conclusion: Electric fields provide a viable route to control friction in layered materials like h-BN, which may have applications in nanoscale devices.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery in physics by exploring models without task-specific fine-tuning.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery in physics, reducing human effort and enabling exploration of diverse physical systems.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of physical systems.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning, demonstrating its generality.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate scientific discovery in physics, potentially accelerating research in the field.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; bridging this gap is necessary to validate quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new computational complexity arguments, including average-case hardness and anticoncentration, tailored to the saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with the number of modes.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible conjectures, extending the theoretical basis for quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for current photonic quantum advantage experiments, confirming that they are indeed hard to simulate classically.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantization of chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons, which are topological excitations in spin chains, and their experimental signatures.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their low-energy excitations and interactions.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental detection methods.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a novel noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the theory while preserving rotational symmetry, and perform numerical simulations.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs on the fuzzy sphere.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying strongly coupled CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such systems.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré materials is important for potential information manipulation, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for designing materials with tailored spin textures, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To predict physical links in networks where direct observation is difficult.
method: Uses a physics-informed approach combining network dynamics and causal inference.
result: The framework successfully infers causal links across various networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed methods can effectively predict network links, with applications in complex systems.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods to study anyon superfluidity.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the three-dimensional XY universality class and nonlinear magnetic susceptibility in a kagome ice compound HoAgGe.
motivation: To investigate hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states of a kagome spin ice system.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements and neutron scattering experiments.
result: Observation of a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and evidence for time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The kagome ice compound HoAgGe exhibits a phase transition consistent with 3D XY universality and hidden symmetry breaking.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but typically require low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe orbital-selective flat bands that persist up to room temperature, with tunability via material composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics and potential applications in quantum devices at practical temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to study the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2 under varying electric and magnetic fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders is demonstrated.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall physics and magnetoelectric effects.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and simulations to investigate the critical properties of a model of spinning particles that form hyperuniform fluids.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show unusual critical behavior, with suppressed fluctuations but high susceptibility at the critical point.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of critical phenomena in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to soft matter physics.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and the resulting complex domain structures.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were applied to Ni₂MnSbO₆ to identify and map the ferro-rotational state and its coupling with polarity and chirality.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to the formation of complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The study reveals a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined ferroic properties, which may have implications for fundamental physics and potential applications.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing for coherent spin control.
motivation: To realize a gate-tunable ballistic spin valve in graphene, enabling coherent spin control via electron optics.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene is used to reveal ballistic spin transport and achieve spin-dependent electron optics.
result: Gate-tunable ballistic spin transport is observed, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene, advancing spintronics but not directly related to the user's research directions.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a tensor network contraction algorithm with exponential convergence corrections to belief propagation.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard; belief propagation provides an approximation but lacks rigorous error bounds.
method: The authors introduce cluster corrections to belief propagation, enabling polynomial-time contraction with provable exponential convergence of approximation errors.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence in approximation error while maintaining polynomial computational cost.
conclusion: The method offers a practical and theoretically grounded approach for tensor network contraction, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and statistical mechanics.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing that includes stages from quantum advantage to fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on the path to useful quantum computing but does not present new technical results.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its approximation is classically hard, motivating a quantum algorithmic approach.
method: The authors design a complete quantum algorithm pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and demonstrating the algorithm's feasibility.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial approximation as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and highlights potential quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rapidly evolving field with many open questions and potential applications.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling forces.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing results from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and topological states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex systems, but a unified framework is lacking.
method: The authors review field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat these systems.
result: The review unifies diverse approaches and demonstrates applications in chemical, ecological, and epidemiological contexts.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unifying tool for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km.
